title: K. Paramasivam Raises LPG Supply Concerns in Great Nicobar
author: Dweep Tulika
description: BJP State Secretary K. Paramasivam raises concerns over the prolonged LPG shortage in Campbell Bay and calls for advance stocking and regular supply.
html:
Campbell Bay | August 19, 2026

BJP State Secretary K. Paramasivam has raised concerns over the prolonged shortage of LPG cylinders in Campbell Bay, Great Nicobar, and urged the authorities to ensure regular supplies to residents of the remote island.

Speaking on the issue, Paramasivam said the last LPG consignment had reportedly reached Campbell Bay on April 24, after which no regular supply had been received. He said around 240 cylinders had subsequently been transported by a Navy vessel, with another consignment of approximately 240 cylinders expected to be sent, but maintained that the quantity was insufficient to meet local requirements.

According to Paramasivam, Campbell Bay requires around 3,000 cylinders to adequately address the shortage. He attributed the disruption primarily to transportation difficulties, noting that vessels serving the area, including Monostar and Shakti, were undergoing dry-dock and survey-related work.

Paramasivam said advance planning could have helped avoid the situation. He suggested that authorities and the concerned shipping agencies should coordinate in advance whenever vessels are scheduled for dry-dock, allowing larger quantities of essential commodities such as LPG to be transported before the disruption.

He also referred to a protest reportedly held by Campbell Bay residents over the shortage. He said residents in remote areas should not be left without essential supplies and stressed the need for greater attention to the southernmost inhabited parts of the islands.

Paramasivam said he had met Civil Supplies Secretary Praveen Ranjan Jha three times regarding the issue and had also met the Indian Oil Corporation terminal manager. He said he requested that the maximum possible number of LPG cylinders be transported on the next available vessels.

He further suggested that, if immediate funds were a constraint for the concerned agency, IOC could consider supplying cylinders to CCS on a credit basis to prevent further delays. He said the transportation of LPG to Campbell Bay could take seven to ten days, making advance stocking essential.

Paramasivam also raised concerns over an alleged shortage of PDS rice in the area and referred to earlier disruptions in the availability of petrol and diesel. He said ensuring uninterrupted access to essential commodities should remain a priority for the administration in remote island communities.

title: ASHA Workers in Andaman Set for Higher Incentives as NHM Approves ₹5,000 Monthly Payment
author: Dweep Tulika
description: NHM approves ₹5,000 monthly incentive for ASHA workers in Andaman, while the Administration processes a separate ₹3,500 monthly share.
html:
Port Blair: ASHA workers in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are set to receive a higher monthly incentive from the National Health Mission (NHM), with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, approving an increase from ₹2,000 to ₹5,000 per month as a special case for the Islands.

The development was communicated by the Andaman & Nicobar Union Territory Health Mission in a point-wise response to a representation made by the Hon’ble Member of Parliament, A&N Islands, Shri Bishnu Pada Ray, through his letter dated 22 July 2026.

According to the Health Mission's response, the enhancement was approved through the Records of Proceedings (RoP) received from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. The approval was cited as a special case considering the geographical location, low population density and disease burden of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

₹5,000 NHM incentive approved

The Health Mission stated that necessary correspondence for releasing the enhanced ₹5,000 monthly NHM incentive for June 2026, along with the remaining incentives for the period from April to June 2026, was in process and would be released at the earliest.

This means the document records an approved enhancement of the NHM component; it does not state that the payments had already been credited to all ASHA workers at the time of the response.

Administration processing additional ₹3,500 share

The response also addresses a separate component of the ASHA incentive.

The Administration's share, which was stated as ₹500 per month, is proposed to be increased to ₹3,500 per month from the State Health Budget of the A&N Administration.

However, unlike the ₹5,000 NHM enhancement, this increase was still under process for approval by the competent authority of the A&N Administration at the time of the letter.

If the proposed ₹3,500 enhancement is approved and implemented, the two components would together amount to ₹8,500 per month. However, the document does not state that ₹8,500 has already been approved as the final monthly incentive.

Air Ambulance proposal under examination

The Health Mission's response also addressed the issue of Air Ambulance Services in the Islands.

It stated that an alternative funding mechanism was being explored because the service was not covered under NHM funding for FY 2026-27.

The response further said that, following directions of the Lieutenant Governor, A&N Islands, a proposal for providing Air Ambulance Services using Defence aircraft was under examination by the A&N Administration.

Action follows MP's representation

The Health Mission's letter was issued in response to MP Bishnu Pada Ray's representation of 22 July 2026 addressed to the Chief Secretary, seeking action on the enhancement of ASHA incentives and operationalisation of Air Ambulance Services.

The communication was issued from the Office of the State Health Society (A&N Islands) and signed by the Joint Mission Director, UT Health Mission.

The letter was also marked to senior officials including the Chief Secretary, Commissioner-cum-Secretary (Health), Secretary (Health)/Mission Director-UTHM and Director of Health Services for information.

What has been approved and what remains pending

The document establishes three separate positions:

IssueStatus according to Health Mission
NHM ASHA incentive: ₹2,000 → ₹5,000Approved by MoHFW as a special case
Release of April–June 2026 incentivesProcess underway
Administration's share: ₹500 → ₹3,500Awaiting competent authority approval
Air Ambulance through Defence aircraftProposal under examination

The development could provide a significant increase in financial support for ASHA workers if both incentive components are ultimately implemented as proposed.

Editorial Note: This report is based on the official Health Mission communication

title: Student Leader Explains Ongoing Protest Against Deemed University Proposal in Andaman
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Student leader Ayush explained the ongoing protest against the proposed deemed university system in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram, 25 February 2026:

Ayush, a student of Andaman Law College and representative of the Students’ Union, spoke to Dweep Tulika during the candle march organised under the Joint Action Forum (JAF), outlining the background, demands, and progression of the ongoing protest against the proposed deemed university system in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Speaking during the gathering at Tiranga Park, Ayush stated that the movement began on February 3 from Andaman Law College, where students first raised concerns regarding the proposed restructuring of colleges in the islands.

He explained that the protest gradually expanded to institutions including JNRM, Tagore Government College, and B.Ed colleges, eventually receiving wider support from students and members of the public across the islands.

Ayush alleged that the decision to place all existing colleges under a deemed university framework was being pursued without proper consultation with students.

“We should have been asked before such a decision was taken. We do not want a deemed university—we demand a Central University,” he stated.

He further argued that affiliation with Pondicherry University, a Central University established through an Act of Parliament, currently ensures a recognised academic standard for students in the islands.

Expressing concern over infrastructure, Ayush pointed out that several educational institutions, including the Law College, have reportedly been functioning without permanent campuses for years.

“If basic facilities are yet to be fully developed, introducing a new system raises serious questions,” he remarked.

Detailing the course of the agitation, Ayush stated that after the initial demonstrations on February 3, protests were organised at multiple colleges, followed by an “Andaman Bandh” which witnessed participation from students and several organisations.

He added that the Joint Action Forum (JAF) was later formed to coordinate the movement collectively with support from political and social organisations.

According to Ayush, the protest has continued for more than three weeks with increasing public participation from various sections of society.

“People across the islands do not want this new system. If reforms are needed, a Central University should be established instead,” he said.

The interaction took place during a peaceful candle march, where participants reiterated demands for reconsideration of the proposal and protection of higher education interests in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume VIII, Issue No. 12, dated 20 March 2026.

title: AAP Public Meeting in Andaman & Nicobar on August 28 at Tiranga Park
author: Dweep Tulika

html:

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Andaman & Nicobar Islands has announced a public meeting in Sri Vijaya Puram on August 28, 2026, inviting Islanders to participate and discuss issues concerning the Islands.

The meeting is scheduled to be held at Tiranga Park, Aberdeen Bazaar, Sri Vijaya Puram, from 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM.

According to the event announcement, the meeting will focus on the party's stated priorities for the Islands, including education, healthcare, government employment, basic infrastructure, water supply, power supply and transportation.

The party has also highlighted its broader political message of “Alternative Politics” and referred to the “Delhi Model” as part of its campaign narrative.

The event invitation also encourages residents interested in joining the AAP's activities in the Islands to contact the party or visit its office.

Public Meeting Details

📅 Date: August 28, 2026

The public meeting comes amid growing political activity in the Islands, with parties increasingly seeking direct engagement with residents over local issues and development priorities.

title: Passenger Alleges Boarding Denied at Neil Jetty Despite Emergency; Dweep Tulika Examines Wider Shipping Complaints
author: Dweep Tulika
description: A passenger alleges he was denied boarding at Neil Jetty despite an emergency. Dweep Tulika is examining wider inter-island shipping complaints.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 11, 2026

A passenger's allegation that he was denied boarding at Neil Jetty despite reaching the terminal shortly after the scheduled departure time and citing an emergency has raised questions about the flexibility of passenger-handling procedures and the quality of inter-island shipping services in the Islands.

According to Abhibhushan Ghosh, he reached Neil Jetty at approximately 1:02 PM on a day when his brother was scheduled to travel to Havelock on the 1 PM sailing because of an emergency situation.

Ghosh said that although the scheduled departure time had passed by approximately two minutes, the vessel had apparently not yet completely departed from the jetty. According to his account, the boarding stairs had been removed but the vessel's rope had not yet been lifted.

He alleges that he requested the ship's personnel to allow his brother to board, citing the emergency circumstances. Ghosh further claims that the boarding point was close to the jetty and that the passenger could potentially have been accommodated without significantly delaying the vessel.

According to Ghosh, the Captain, Second Officer and other vessel personnel refused to allow boarding. He also claims that police and other personnel present at the jetty repeatedly requested the ship's staff to permit the passenger to board, but the request was not accepted.

These claims have not yet been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

The larger question is how are emergency cases handled?

The incident raises a broader question about whether existing passenger-handling procedures provide any mechanism for dealing with genuine emergencies when a passenger reaches a vessel immediately after the scheduled boarding or departure time but the vessel remains physically at the jetty.

Safety and operational requirements remain fundamental to vessel departures, and the decision of the master and crew may be governed by operational, security and passenger-manifest considerations.

At the same time, the absence of publicly established information about the precise cut-off procedure makes it difficult to determine whether an exception could legally or operationally have been made in the particular case.

Dweep Tulika has received other shipping complaints

The Neil Jetty complaint is not the only concern that has come to Dweep Tulika.

The newspaper has been examining complaints concerning inter-island passenger shipping, including a separate complaint involving MV Sentinel, in which a member of the Dweep Tulika team and their family allegedly were unable to board the vessel while attempting to travel to Diglipur to visit ill parents.

Dweep Tulika has also received complaints alleging:

  • ticket resale or brokering at prices higher than the prescribed fare;
  • discrepancies between actual ticket availability and availability displayed through online booking;
  • non-functional or poorly maintained bathrooms;
  • air-conditioning problems;
  • poor vessel conditions;
  • and insufficient availability of vessels for passenger demand.

These are complaints received by Dweep Tulika and are not being presented as established findings.

The Directorate of Shipping Services operates an e-ticketing system for passenger bookings, while STARS counters also issue tickets. Official sailing information has also documented MV Sentinel's deployment on inter-island routes.

Questions requiring answers

Taken together, the complaints raise several questions that warrant responses from the Directorate of Shipping Services and other concerned authorities:

What is the official boarding cut-off time for passengers?

Is there a documented emergency exception procedure?

Are CCTV recordings maintained at passenger jetties and retained long enough to investigate complaints?

How are passenger manifests closed before departure?

How are complaints regarding unauthorised ticket resale investigated?

What mechanism exists for reporting discrepancies between online ticket availability and actual availability?

How frequently are passenger vessels inspected for passenger amenities and maintenance deficiencies?

What is the present vessel capacity against passenger demand on major inter-island routes?

These questions are particularly relevant in an island territory where sea transport is not merely a convenience but an essential link between communities.

A service that Islanders depend on

Official and government planning material has previously recognised a demand-supply gap in inter-island vessel services, highlighting the importance of adequate vessel capacity.

For Islanders travelling for medical treatment, education, employment, family emergencies and other essential purposes, a missed sailing can have consequences far beyond inconvenience.

The question arising from the Neil Jetty complaint is therefore not simply whether a passenger who arrived two minutes after scheduled departure should have been allowed aboard.

It is also whether clear, transparent and consistently applied procedures exist for handling exceptional circumstances and whether passengers have an effective mechanism to challenge decisions when they believe those procedures have not been fairly applied.

Dweep Tulika will seek responses from the Directorate of Shipping Services, the concerned vessel operator/master and other relevant authorities regarding the Neil Jetty incident and the wider complaints received by the newspaper.

Independent verification could not be established at the time of publication for the allegations made by the complainant or for the broader passenger-service complaints. The concerned authorities' responses will be incorporated as and when received.

title: TSG Bhasker Distributes Fruit Kits to Patients at Ayush Hospital on Rahul Gandhi's Birthday
author: Dweep Tulika
description: TSG Bhasker distributed fruit kits to patients at Ayush Hospital, Junglighat, on the birthday of Rahul Gandhi.
html:

Shri TSG Bhasker, Chairman of the Campaign Committee of the Andaman & Nicobar Territorial Congress Committee (ANTCC), distributed fruit kits to patients admitted at Ayush Hospital, Junglighat, on the occasion of the birthday of Shri Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

As part of the observance, Shri Bhasker visited the hospital and interacted with patients and their attendants. He enquired about their well-being and wished them a speedy recovery.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Bhasker stated that the best way to celebrate the birthday of a leader who has consistently stood with the people is by extending support and care to those in need.

title: Thousands of CBSE Class 12 students saw higher marks after re-evaluation under the board's new digital assessment system.
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Thousands of CBSE Class 12 students saw higher marks after re-evaluation under the board's new digital assessment system.
html:
Thousands of CBSE Class 12 students recorded higher scores after the board re-evaluated answer sheets following concerns over its new digital evaluation process.

New Delhi, June 23:

Thousands of CBSE Class 12 students have witnessed a significant increase in their examination scores after the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) completed the re-evaluation of answer sheets under its newly introduced digital assessment system.

According to CBSE, nearly 1.6 lakh students applied for re-evaluation after concerns were raised regarding discrepancies in the evaluation process. On June 21, the board released revised results for around 1.39 lakh candidates, while the remaining results are expected to be declared in phases.

The issue surfaced after the introduction of the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluating answer sheets during the 2026 examination cycle. Several students reported problems such as blurry scanned answer sheets, missing pages, absent maps or graphs, and instances where answers were allegedly evaluated using marking schemes meant for different question paper sets.

Following the review process, many students saw noticeable improvements in their marks, raising fresh discussions about the implementation and quality control of digital evaluation systems.

Education experts have observed that while digital assessment offers advantages such as faster processing and improved record management, it also requires robust quality checks to ensure fairness and accuracy.

CBSE has stated that the remaining re-evaluation results will be announced shortly. The board also said it is working to address concerns related to the digital evaluation system and strengthen transparency and reliability in future examination assessments.

title: ₹250 for Five Months: South Point Residents Question Garbage Collection Service
author: Dweep Tulika
description: South Point residents question a ₹250 five-month waste-management charge and seek clarity on door-to-door garbage collection and service standards.
html:
Residents say household waste is not consistently collected from doorsteps and seek clarity on the service attached to the municipal user fee

Sri Vijaya Puram, September 11, 2026:

Residents of South Point have raised questions over the collection of a ₹250 household waste-management charge for five months, particularly regarding the manner in which garbage collection is being carried out in parts of the locality.

A digital payment receipt shared with Dweep Tulika shows a payment of ₹250 to the Municipal Council on September 11, 2026. Residents describe the payment as a charge associated with household waste collection, which works out to ₹50 per month.

While user fees form part of the solid-waste management framework, residents are questioning whether the service being delivered corresponds with what they understand as door-to-door garbage collection. The Solid Waste Management Rules provide for user fees as specified in local-body bye-laws and also provide for door-to-door collection of waste.

According to residents, garbage is not consistently collected from the doorstep of every house in South Point. In some compounds, households reportedly have to bring their waste to the entrance or hand it over to collection workers when they reach the roadside.

The concern is particularly relevant for houses located away from the main road. Residents said collection workers had earlier used a whistle to alert households that the garbage collection team had arrived, allowing residents to bring their waste out for collection.

They now allege that even this practice has become irregular, with whistles reportedly not being used consistently.

Residents also claim that insufficient sanitation staff are being deployed in some stretches of South Point, making regular collection difficult.

This has led residents to question what constitutes “door-to-door” collection in practice.

If households are required to carry their waste to a common point or the roadside before it is collected, residents want to know whether that arrangement is consistent with the service for which the household charge is being collected.

The issue also raises questions about the distinction between municipal taxes, conservancy-related charges and user fees for solid-waste management.

Residents who own property already make various payments to the municipality and government. They therefore want greater clarity on what the additional household waste-management fee specifically finances and what service standard is attached to it.

The questions being raised by residents include:

  • What is the official basis for the ₹250 charge?
  • Why is the charge collected for a five-month period?
  • What is the prescribed frequency of household waste collection?
  • Does “door-to-door” collection require collection from every household, or are residents expected to bring waste to designated collection points?
  • How many sanitation workers are assigned to South Point?
  • What mechanism exists when a household is missed?
  • How does SVPMC monitor whether the service is actually being delivered?

The issue, therefore, is not simply about the amount of ₹250.

It concerns the relationship between user charges and service delivery.

A user fee is part of the solid-waste management financing framework, but the exact fee, collection mechanism and service obligations applicable to a particular municipal area depend on the relevant local-body provisions.

Dweep Tulika seeks clarification from SVPMC on the ₹250 charge, the five-month collection cycle, the number of sanitation workers deployed in South Point, the prescribed method and frequency of household collection, and the mechanism available to residents when their household is not reached.

The allegations regarding irregular collection, whistle use and staffing are based on residents' accounts and have not been independently established by Dweep Tulika. A response from SVPMC should be incorporated when received.

For residents, the central question remains straightforward:

If a household is being charged specifically for waste-management services, what service is the municipality required to provide and is that service reaching every household that is being charged?

title: AAP’s Arun Kumar Mallik Seeks Follow-Up on NHIDCL Action Report, Pushes for Additional NH-4 Weighbridges
author: Dweep Tulika
description: AAP leader Arun Kumar Mallik seeks follow-up on NHIDCL recommendations for NH-4 weighbridges, vehicle-load restrictions and enforcement.
html:
Port Blair: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Andaman & Nicobar Islands State President Dr Arun Kumar Mallik has urged the Andaman & Nicobar Administration to follow up on recommendations and actions proposed by the National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL) concerning enforcement against overloaded commercial goods vehicles and the construction of additional weighbridges along National Highway-4 (NH-4).

In a letter dated 7 September 2026 addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, South Andaman District, Mallik referred to an earlier request regarding an additional weighbridge on NH-4, mandatory use of the existing Mile Tilak weighbridge by commercial goods vehicles, exemption of weighbridge user fees for vehicles transporting fresh vegetables, and continuation of the 12-tonne maximum truck-load restriction on vehicle ferries.

Mallik said NHIDCL had provided technical comments and an Action Taken Report (ATR), including recommendations from its technical experts and engineers, following his earlier correspondence. He described the recommendations as feasible and said several could be implemented immediately, except for the construction of an additional weighbridge.

Call for continued enforcement against overloaded vehicles

Mallik urged the Administration to continue enforcement against overloaded commercial goods vehicles, citing the need to protect the pavement, bridges, culverts and other highway assets.

He acknowledged the role of the Regional Transport Office, Directorate of State Transport Services and other enforcement agencies in the ongoing drives.

He also requested a fresh verification of the operation, legal status and calibration of the weighbridge at Mile Tilak, and called for its mandatory use by every commercial goods vehicle travelling on NH-4.

12-tonne ferry-load restriction

Mallik further called for continuation of the restriction limiting the maximum truck load of commercial goods vehicles to 12 tonnes on vehicle ferries.

He said the Directorate of Shipping Services and Port Management Board were enforcing the restriction and urged that it continue.

Proposal for additional weighbridges

Beyond the existing facility at Mile Tilak, Mallik proposed consideration of additional weighbridges at several locations.

He identified Garacharama/Port Blair, Nimbutala/Rangat, Tugapur/Mayabunder and Sitanagar/Diglipur as locations that, in his view, could benefit from additional public-accessible weighbridges.

He called for a feasibility study to identify critical hubs, particularly trans-island entry and exit points.

Mallik also suggested either a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model or an Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) approach, along with consultation with local truck and cargo associations. He proposed coordination between NHIDCL, State Transport Services, the Directorate of Shipping Services and the district administrations.

NH-4 completion timeline cited

In the letter, Mallik said that following a meeting with NHIDCL's Executive Director, he had learnt that construction of the entire NH-4 was expected to be completed by March 2027, while the second bridge was expected by mid-2028, subject to timely availability of construction materials, particularly bitumen.

He described the availability of bitumen as a challenge being faced by NHIDCL.

The completion timelines are presented here as information conveyed to Mallik and cited in his letter, rather than as independently verified project deadlines.

Earlier communication with NHIDCL

The uploaded correspondence also contains a 2 September communication from Mallik to NHIDCL thanking the organisation for its response and for providing recommendations and details concerning actions taken on his requests. Mallik said he intended to take those recommendations forward with relevant departments, particularly State Transport Services and the Directorate of Shipping Services.

The correspondence refers to two annexures from NHIDCL, including a letter dated 31 August 2026 and an Action Taken Report concerning the proposed additional NH-04 weighbridge and continued enforcement. The actual substantive contents of those annexures are not reproduced in the parsed text available here.

title: International Yoga Day 2026 Celebrated Across India with Focus on Healthy Ageing
author: Dweep Tulika
description: India celebrated the 12th International Yoga Day with the theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing' and nationwide participation.
html:
Millions participated in International Yoga Day 2026 celebrations across India and abroad under the theme "Yoga for Healthy Ageing."

New Delhi/Kolkata, June 21:

India marked the 12th International Yoga Day on Sunday with large-scale events held across the country and around the world. This year's theme, "Yoga for Healthy Ageing," emphasized the role of yoga in promoting physical fitness, mental well-being and active lifestyles throughout life.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the main International Yoga Day event at Red Road in Kolkata, West Bengal, where thousands of participants gathered for a mass yoga session. Similar events were organised in cities, towns and villages across India, while yoga enthusiasts in many countries also took part in celebrations.

Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Modi highlighted the importance of incorporating yoga into daily life. He said that yoga helps individuals maintain physical health, mental strength and overall well-being as they grow older.

The Prime Minister also described yoga as a universal practice that brings people together beyond differences of language, culture, religion and nationality.
According to the Ministry of AYUSH, the theme "Yoga for Healthy Ageing" was chosen to promote awareness about healthy lifestyles, disease prevention and improved quality of life among people of all age groups.

Yoga Day programmes were organised at thousands of locations across India and abroad, reflecting the continued global acceptance and popularity of yoga as a tool for health and wellness.
International Yoga Day has been observed annually on June 21 since 2015 after the United Nations adopted a proposal introduced by India to recognise yoga as a global movement promoting health, harmony and well-being.
This year's celebrations witnessed enthusiastic participation from citizens, students, yoga practitioners, community groups and organisations, reinforcing the message of healthy living through yoga and holistic wellness.

title: Why Andaman Doesn't Feel Like Just Another Indian Territory
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Why governing the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is unlike any other part of India, from geography and defence to tribal protection.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | July 6, 2026

Imagine governing a place where every sack of cement, every litre of fuel, every ambulance, and even many government officials must first cross more than 1,200 kilometres of sea before reaching their destination.

Welcome to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India's most isolated and perhaps most uniquely administered Union Territory.

For many visitors, the islands feel almost like another country. Flights from mainland India take several hours, ships require days, and daily life is shaped less by highways and railways than by tides, weather conditions and ferry schedules. Yet these islands remain an inseparable part of India, making their administration unlike anywhere else in the country.

Unlike Indian states, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands do not have a Legislative Assembly or an elected Chief Minister. Instead, the Union Territory is administered by the Lieutenant Governor on behalf of the Central Government. As a result, many important decisions from infrastructure development and public services to long-term policy planning require close coordination with New Delhi.

Geography itself presents the administration's greatest challenge.

Rather than being a single island, the territory consists of hundreds of islands scattered across hundreds of kilometres. Delivering healthcare, education, electricity, drinking water, policing, internet connectivity and other essential public services to such dispersed populations requires logistical planning unlike that of almost any other region in India.

Even routine governance becomes extraordinary.

A damaged power transformer cannot simply be transported by road from a neighbouring district. Medicines, construction materials, heavy machinery and emergency relief supplies often depend on sea or air transport. Adverse weather can delay everything from school textbooks to life-saving medical equipment.

The islands are equally significant from a strategic perspective.

Situated close to the Strait of Malacca, one of the world's busiest maritime trade routes, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands serve as a critical pillar of India's maritime security. Defence requirements frequently influence decisions relating to infrastructure, ports, aviation facilities and land use in ways rarely seen elsewhere in the country.

Adding to these responsibilities is the need to protect some of the world's oldest surviving indigenous communities. Policymakers must carefully balance development, conservation, tourism and the rights of protected tribal groups while preserving fragile ecosystems recognised for their global ecological importance.

Natural disasters present another unique governance challenge.

Earthquakes, cyclones and the lasting memory of the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami serve as constant reminders that disaster preparedness is not merely an administrative responsibility but a necessity for survival.

Perhaps what makes the Andaman and Nicobar Islands truly exceptional is that they do not fit neatly into any conventional administrative model.

They are geographically remote, culturally diverse, strategically vital, environmentally sensitive and heavily dependent on maritime and air connectivity. Effective governance therefore demands continuous coordination among the civilian administration, local self-government institutions, the armed forces and the Central Government.

For many residents, the distance from mainland India can sometimes create the feeling of living in a different country.

In reality, the islands represent one of India's most remarkable governance challenges, where nearly every policy, project and public service must first cross the sea before reaching the people.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are not simply another Union Territory.

They may well represent India's most extraordinary administrative story.


Report By: R. Vineeth, Editor-in-Chief, Dweep Tulika

title: Vance Says Iran Talks Have Laid ‘Good Foundation’ for Peace Deal
author: Dweep Tulika
description: JD Vance says U.S.-Iran talks in Switzerland have laid a strong foundation for a future agreement aimed at ending regional conflict.
html:
U.S. Vice President JD Vance says recent negotiations with Iranian officials in Switzerland have created a strong foundation for a future agreement aimed at reducing regional tensions and ending the conflict.

Obbuergen, Switzerland, June 23:

U.S. Vice President JD Vance has described recent talks with senior Iranian officials in Switzerland as a positive step towards ending the ongoing regional conflict, saying the discussions have established a "good foundation" for a future peace agreement.

The negotiations, held over several hours in Obbuergen, focused on regional security, maritime stability, and confidence-building measures designed to reduce tensions between the two countries.

Speaking after the meeting, Vance said that although a final agreement has not yet been reached, both sides had made meaningful progress and identified areas where further negotiations could continue.

The discussions also addressed security concerns surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important maritime trade routes through which a significant portion of global oil shipments passes.

According to U.S. officials, technical-level discussions will continue in the coming weeks as negotiators work towards a broader and more comprehensive agreement.

The latest diplomatic engagement comes amid sustained international efforts to reduce tensions in the Middle East following months of instability and military confrontation.

Observers believe that continued dialogue between Washington and Tehran could play an important role in improving regional stability, although several complex issues remain unresolved before any final agreement can be concluded.

title: Shyam Rangeela Brings Political Satire to Gen Z Protest in New Delhi
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Comedian Shyam Rangeela's satirical performance at the Gen Z protest in New Delhi sparks discussion on political satire and democratic expression.
html:
NEW DELHI, July 24:

Comedian and politician Shyam Rangeela (born Shyam Sunder on 25 August 1994 in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan) briefly took the microphone during the ongoing Gen Z protest in New Delhi and delivered a satirical performance by mimicking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's voice.

In his act, Rangeela referenced several promises made before past elections, using humour and imitation to comment on political accountability. The performance quickly drew attention on social media, with supporters describing it as a memorable example of political satire, while others debated its message and timing.

Political satire has long been a part of democratic societies, offering a way to question those in power through humour, parody and public expression. Like other forms of speech, it often attracts both appreciation and criticism.

The performance became one of several moments from the ongoing demonstrations that circulated widely online, reflecting the diverse forms of expression seen during public protests.

Democracy speaks in many forms. Sometimes, it laughs.

title: JNV Teacher Dies After Being Swept Away by Waves in Car Nicobar on Holi
author: Dweep Tulika
description: A JNV teacher in Car Nicobar died after being swept away by strong waves near Arong village during Holi celebrations.
html:
Car Nicobar, 04 March 26:

A tragic incident was reported on the occasion of Holi, where a teacher of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya (JNV), Car Nicobar, lost her life after being swept away by strong waves near a beach at Arong village.

The deceased has been identified as Ms. Renuka, who was serving as a teacher at JNV Car Nicobar.

According to sources, a group comprising five teachers along with the son of the school principal had gone to the beach during the morning hours. While they were near the shore, three individuals were suddenly swept away by powerful waves. Local residents present at the site managed to rescue two of them.

However, Ms. Renuka was carried further into the sea by strong currents. She was later retrieved with the assistance of an Indian Air Force helicopter and airlifted to the Air Force Station at Car Nicobar.

She was subsequently taken to BJR Hospital in the headquarters area, where doctors declared her brought dead.

Sources stated that Ms. Renuka did not have immediate family members in Car Nicobar, with her family reportedly residing in Sri Vijaya Puram.

It is learnt that the group had not entered the sea for swimming; however, the exact circumstances under which the waves swept them away remain unclear. Further details regarding the incident are awaited.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume VIII, Issue No. 12, dated 20 March 2026.

title: Opposition Plans to Urge Immediate Implementation of Women’s Reservation Law
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Opposition parties plan to urge the Prime Minister to implement the Women’s Reservation Law without waiting for delimitation.
html:
April 18, 2026 | New Delhi

Opposition parties are preparing to write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the immediate implementation of the women’s reservation law passed in 2023 by separating it from the delimitation process.

Leaders argue that linking the law’s rollout to delimitation could lead to delays and have called for its enforcement without waiting for constituency reorganisation.

The issue was discussed at a meeting held in New Delhi on April 18, 2026, where Congress president and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, chaired a gathering of floor leaders from parties aligned with the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) bloc.

During the meeting, there was broad agreement among participating leaders on pressing for the immediate operationalisation of reservation for women in legislative bodies.

Opposition leaders reportedly maintained that the law, having already received parliamentary approval, should be implemented without being tied to future delimitation exercises.

The development signals a renewed political push on the issue of women’s representation in elected institutions and is expected to remain a subject of debate in the coming months.

title: Srishti Gupta’s Andaman Visit Raises Questions Beyond an Instagram Caption
author: Dweep Tulika
html:
Her meetings with senior officials come amid renewed scrutiny of Great Nicobar, a leadership transition at Raj Niwas and a fresh push for strategic and energy infrastructure

Sri Vijayapuram: A recent social-media post by Haryana-cadre IPS officer Srishti Gupta about her meeting with Admiral D.K. Joshi at Raj Niwas has drawn attention beyond the meeting itself.

Gupta's public posts about her visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands refer to interactions with senior defence officers and discuss themes including national security, ecological sensitivity and development.

Her post about meeting Admiral D.K. Joshi also described him as the “Chairman of Islands Development Authority” and referred to his tenure as Lieutenant Governor as “10 years”.

Those descriptions require correction.

The official body is the Islands Development Agency (IDA), not “Islands Development Authority”. Government records identify the Union Home Minister as chairing the IDA, while Admiral Joshi served as its Vice-Chairman.

Joshi assumed office as Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on 8 October 2017. As of September 2026, his tenure was therefore approaching nine years, rather than ten.

These may appear to be minor inaccuracies in a social-media post. But the timing of the visit and the subjects discussed make the wider context worth examining.

Why the timing matters

On 25 August 2026, the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) adopted its concluding observations on India's combined twentieth and twenty-first periodic reports.

The Committee specifically expressed concern over reported impacts of development projects on Great Nicobar and the Andaman Islands, including possible effects on vulnerable Indigenous peoples. It recommended that projects on Great Nicobar and the Andaman Islands be suspended until a full and independent environmental, economic, social, cultural and spiritual impact study had been completed.

The recommendation should be described accurately: it is a recommendation of a UN treaty body, not an international court order or an injunction halting the project.

India rejected the Committee's observations, describing some of the references as politically motivated.

The development therefore represents international scrutiny of the Islands' development policies, while the Government of India continues to describe the Great Nicobar project as being of strategic, defence and national importance.

Leadership change at Raj Niwas

Another major development followed on 5 September 2026, when the President of India announced the appointment of Dr Dinesh Sharma as the next Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The appointment takes effect from the date he assumes office.

Admiral D.K. Joshi had held the Lieutenant Governor's office since 8 October 2017.

There is currently no evidence establishing that the leadership change was caused by the UN observations, the Great Nicobar project or any controversy surrounding Indigenous rights.

The timing is nevertheless notable because it comes amid a period of substantial policy and infrastructure activity in the Islands.

That makes it a subject for questions—not conclusions.

Great Nicobar's mainland connection

The Great Nicobar project also has a mainland environmental connection that deserves attention.

According to a Government of India backgrounder, because the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have more than 75% forest cover, compensatory afforestation for forest diversion is being undertaken outside the Union Territory. The government says Haryana and Madhya Pradesh have been identified for substantial portions of this compensatory afforestation, with about 17,000 hectares in Haryana and 6,320.10 hectares in Madhya Pradesh.

This creates an important ecological debate.

The government's position is that compensatory afforestation follows the applicable legal framework and provides ecological compensation. Critics, however, question whether plantations or restoration on mainland land can replicate the ecological functions of an island ecosystem such as Great Nicobar.

That is ultimately an environmental and scientific question—not something that can be settled merely by comparing the number of hectares planted elsewhere.

The strategic push continues

The scale of development planned for Great Nicobar is not in dispute.

Government documents describe the project as including an International Container Transshipment Terminal, a Greenfield International Airport, a 450 MVA power plant and a township. The government explicitly describes the project as having strategic, defence and national-security significance.

The Government of India says the project is intended to strengthen India's presence in the Andaman Sea and Southeast Asia while integrating the Islands into international trade and logistics networks.

The Islands' military significance also predates the current project.

INS Baaz, commissioned in Great Nicobar in 2012, was described by the Defence Ministry as strategically important because of its position overlooking the Strait of Malacca and the Six Degree Channel.

Similarly, INS Kohassa in North Andaman was commissioned as a naval air station in 2019, with the Defence Ministry describing its location as strategically important for the security of the Islands and the operational capabilities of the Andaman and Nicobar Command.

So the argument that the Islands have become strategically important should not be presented as a recent development. What is new is the scale and combination of economic, energy and infrastructure projects now being pursued alongside that long-standing strategic role.

And then there is BARC

Another significant development occurred during the same period.

A team of scientists from the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) under the Department of Atomic Energy visited the Islands from 4 to 8 September 2026 to inspect potential sites for proposed Small Modular Reactors (SMRs).

The team reportedly inspected locations across all three districts and met Admiral Joshi on 4 September, presenting information on potential sites. The stated rationale was to meet the rising power requirements associated with major infrastructure projects.

The projects cited in connection with the power requirement include the proposed transshipment terminal, greenfield airport, deep-water multipurpose ports and other major infrastructure.

This is a proposal for civilian power generation. It should not be presented as evidence of a nuclear-weapons programme or military nuclear deployment.

What it does demonstrate is that the scale of future electricity demand being contemplated for the Islands is substantial enough for SMR sites to now be examined.

What about Joshi's military record?

Gupta's post praises Admiral Joshi's “grit and determination” and refers to his identity as a “fauji at heart.”

His earlier career as Chief of Naval Staff also includes a difficult period for the Indian Navy.

In February 2014, Joshi resigned as Chief of Naval Staff, with the Ministry of Defence stating that he was taking moral responsibility for accidents and incidents that had occurred in the preceding months.

Among the incidents during that period was the 2013 sinking of INS Sindhurakshak, in which 18 personnel died. The subsequent INS Sindhuratna accident in February 2014 also contributed to the circumstances surrounding his resignation.

That history should not be turned into a claim that Joshi personally caused those accidents.

The more accurate point is narrower: Joshi accepted moral responsibility and resigned while serving as Navy Chief.

That is relevant context when evaluating a public discussion of his military leadership, but it does not by itself determine his record as Lieutenant Governor.

So why was Srishti Gupta in Andaman?

This remains the most interesting unanswered question.

Gupta is indeed a Haryana-cadre IPS officer. Government records identify her as a 2021-batch Haryana-cadre IPS officer, and the Haryana Police currently lists her as an AIG/Welfare.

Her public professional profile also contains a post describing what she learnt from Major General Ajay Feroze Shah, Chief of Staff of the Andaman and Nicobar Command, including lessons concerning military discipline, remote postings and the challenge of balancing ecological sensitivity with national security.

She also referred to interactions with other Army and Navy personnel.

However, I could not locate a publicly available official document establishing the purpose, sponsorship or institutional programme behind her visit to the Islands.

That does not make the visit suspicious.

It simply means that an important piece of context remains unavailable.

If the visit was part of an official training, familiarisation, inter-governmental, professional or institutional programme, establishing that would materially change how the meetings should be understood.

More questions than conclusions

It is tempting, given the timing, to connect the UN's concerns over Great Nicobar, the transition at Raj Niwas, the BARC site inspections, the Islands' strategic infrastructure and Gupta's meetings with senior officials into a single narrative.

The evidence available at present does not justify that conclusion.

But the individual developments are real.

The Government of India is continuing to advance a major Great Nicobar infrastructure programme that it explicitly describes as strategically important.

A UN treaty body has raised concerns about the impact of projects on Indigenous peoples and recommended their suspension pending independent impact studies.

A new Lieutenant Governor has been appointed after Admiral Joshi's nearly nine-year tenure.

And BARC scientists have inspected possible locations for Small Modular Reactors to support the Islands' projected energy requirements.

Against that backdrop, several questions are legitimate:

What will be the next phase of the Great Nicobar project?

How will environmental and Indigenous concerns be addressed alongside strategic and economic objectives?

Why was a Haryana-cadre IPS officer visiting the Islands and meeting senior defence and administrative figures, and under what institutional capacity?

What will the transition from Admiral D.K. Joshi to Dr Dinesh Sharma mean for the next phase of governance and development?

And perhaps the most important question:

How will the Islands balance strategic ambition and economic development with the ecological and Indigenous sensitivities that make the territory unlike any ordinary infrastructure zone?

For now, the evidence supports the questions.

It does not yet support the conclusions.

title: RTI Reveals Centre Spent ₹2,585.80 Crore on Government Advertisements in Six Financial Years; Vendor-Wise Payments Withheld
author: Dweep Tulika
description: RTI reveals the Centre spent ₹2,585.80 crore on government advertisements through CBC since FY 2020-21. Vendor-wise payments were withheld.
html:
RTI Reveals Centre Spent ₹2,585.80 Crore on Government Advertisements in Six Financial Years; Vendor-Wise Payments Withheld

By Dweep Tulika News Desk

New Delhi / Sri Vijaya Puram | July 11

An official reply obtained under the Right to Information (RTI) Act has revealed that the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) under the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting spent ₹2,585.80 crore on government advertisements across print, television, radio, outdoor publicity and digital media between FY 2020-21 and 11 June 2026.

The information was disclosed in response to RTI Registration No. DOAVP/R/T/26/00095, filed by Rajya Sabha MP Saket Gokhale. The reply, dated 16 June 2026, includes detailed year-wise expenditure across different media categories.

How Was the Expenditure Distributed?

According to Annexure A of the RTI reply:

Media CategoryExpenditure
Television & Radio₹935.90 crore
Print Media₹795.86 crore
Outdoor Publicity₹584.97 crore
Digital / New Media₹269.07 crore
Total₹2,585.80 crore

Based on the total expenditure disclosed in the RTI, the government spent an average of approximately:

  • ₹431 crore per year
  • ₹35.9 crore per month
  • ₹1.18 crore per day

during the period covered by the RTI.

Expenditure Increased in Recent Years

The RTI records indicate a significant increase in advertising expenditure over time.

Print media expenditure rose from approximately ₹53.77 crore in FY 2020-21 to nearly ₹338 crore in FY 2025-26.

Digital and New Media spending also increased substantially, rising from ₹14.40 crore to ₹131.35 crore during the same period.

Outdoor publicity expenditure increased notably after FY 2022-23, while Television & Radio remained the largest category of expenditure throughout the reporting period.

Agency-Wise Payment Details Withheld

The RTI applicant also requested details regarding payments made to individual advertising agencies.

The Central Bureau of Communication declined to disclose those records, citing Section 8(1)(d) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, which exempts certain commercial information from disclosure if releasing it could harm the competitive position of a third party.

Consequently, the names of advertising agencies and vendor-wise payment details were not disclosed.

Under the RTI Act, such decisions may be challenged through the prescribed appeal process before the appropriate appellate authority or the Central Information Commission.

Scope of the RTI

The expenditure disclosed relates only to advertisements released through the Central Bureau of Communication, the Government of India's nodal agency for public communication campaigns.

The RTI does not include:

  • Political party expenditure.
  • Election campaign spending.
  • Advertisements issued by State Governments.
  • Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) publicity.
  • Advertisements released independently by other government departments or agencies outside the scope of this RTI.

Transparency and Public Accountability

Government advertising serves multiple public purposes, including awareness campaigns, dissemination of welfare schemes, health advisories, disaster information and official policy communication.

As public funds are involved, such expenditure is subject to scrutiny under the Right to Information Act.

While the RTI provides verified information regarding the total expenditure incurred through the CBC, it does not identify the individual agencies that received payments. Whether greater transparency regarding the distribution of these public funds should be provided remains a matter that may be examined through the RTI appeals process or by the Central Information Commission.

RTI Snapshot

Ministry: Information & Broadcasting

RTI Registration No.: DOAVP/R/T/26/00095

CategoryExpenditure

Print₹795.86 crore

Digital / New Media₹269.07 crore
Total₹2,585.80 crore

title: Mukta Dhara Society Urges SVPMC to Improve Public Dustbins and Waste Management
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Mukta Dhara Society has urged SVPMC to install more public dustbins and strengthen sanitation under the Become the Change, Clean Andaman Initiative.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar Islands | 6 August 2026

Mukta Dhara Society has submitted a representation to the Secretary, Sri Vijaya Puram Municipal Council (SVPMC) seeking the installation of additional public dustbins and improvements in sanitation and solid waste management as part of its "Become the Change – Clean Andaman Initiative," being conducted in collaboration with Dweep Tulika News. 

In the representation, the Society stated that interactions with residents across various wards had highlighted concerns regarding the inadequate availability of public dustbins in markets, parks, beaches, bus stops and other high-footfall areas. It also referred to complaints about open garbage collection points, which were said to attract stray animals and contribute to scattered waste, foul odours and unhygienic conditions. 

To address these concerns, Mukta Dhara Society requested the Municipal Council to install covered twin dustbins for wet and dry waste at prominent public locations, replace open community garbage collection points with enclosed or animal-proof systems wherever feasible, ensure timely collection of waste, deploy adequate sanitation staff for regular inspections, strengthen enforcement against littering under the relevant municipal bye-laws, and install awareness signage promoting proper waste disposal and segregation. 

The Society stated that coordinated efforts by government departments, local bodies, civil society organisations and citizens are essential for building a cleaner, healthier and more environmentally conscious Andaman. It also reaffirmed its commitment, along with DT News, to continue supporting public awareness campaigns and community engagement under the initiative. 

Copies of the representation have been forwarded to the Chairperson of the Sri Vijaya Puram Municipal Council, the Public Health Officer, the Assistant Engineer (Solid Waste Management), the Deputy Commissioner of South Andaman, the Member Secretary of the Pollution Control Committee, the concerned Ward Councillors, the Director of Panchayats & Municipal Bodies, and other stakeholders for information and necessary action.

title: Congress Seeks Answers on Great Nicobar Transhipment Port Project
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Congress has sought details from the Centre on ownership, bidding and transparency in the Great Nicobar Transhipment Port project.
html:
Congress has sought detailed clarification from the Centre on the proposed International Container Transhipment Port at Great Nicobar, raising questions on ownership, private participation and transparency.

New Delhi, June 23:

The Congress has sought greater clarity from the Central Government regarding the proposed International Container Transhipment Port at Galathea Bay in Great Nicobar Island, raising questions over the project's ownership structure, bidding process and private sector participation.

Congress General Secretary Jairam Ramesh has written tpo Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal, seeking detailed information on how the project will be implemented.

In his letter, Ramesh asked when tenders for the project would be issued and when the private operator and co-owner of the proposed port would be selected. He also sought clarification on the maximum level of private shareholding permitted and the safeguards being put in place to ensure transparency and fair competition during the bidding process.

The Congress leader also expressed concern over the environmental implications of the broader Great Nicobar Development Project, which includes an international container transhipment port, an international airport, a township and a power plant.

He stressed the need for greater public transparency, accountability and disclosure of information related to one of India's largest infrastructure projects.

The Central Government has consistently maintained that the Great Nicobar Project is of strategic and economic importance. According to the government, the project will strengthen India's maritime security, reduce dependence on foreign transhipment hubs, enhance trade competitiveness and generate economic opportunities, while ensuring environmental safeguards and protection of indigenous communities.

The Great Nicobar Project continues to remain the subject of public and political debate, with supporters highlighting its strategic significance and critics raising environmental and ecological concerns.

The Centre has not yet publicly responded to the specific questions raised in the latest letter.

title: Sonam Wangchuk Ends 26-Day Fast; NEET Protest Movement Continues Across India
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Sonam Wangchuk ends his 26-day hunger strike after talks are agreed, but nationwide protests over examination reforms continue.
html:
NEW DELHI, July 24: 

Activist Sonam Wangchuk has ended his 26-day hunger strike after the Central Government agreed to hold talks with representatives of the student movement, marking a significant development in the ongoing nationwide protests over alleged examination paper leaks. 

Despite Wangchuk calling off his fast, protest organisers have announced that demonstrations will continue across Delhi and several other states until concrete reforms are implemented. Today's nationwide campaign is being held under the slogan "Every District. One Day. One Demand." According to organisers, the movement continues to seek action against alleged examination paper leaks, comprehensive education reforms, accountability for recent police action against demonstrators, and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. 

Security arrangements have been significantly strengthened in the national capital. According to official announcements, 17 Delhi Metro stations remain closed, mobile internet services have been restricted around Jantar Mantar, and additional police personnel have been deployed across central Delhi in view of the continuing demonstrations. 

The Central Government has announced several measures to address examination-related concerns, including proposals for stricter anti-paper leak legislation and fast-track courts to deal with such cases. However, protest organisers have stated that these measures are insufficient without broader structural reforms to the examination system. 

Meanwhile, reports of police action during recent demonstrations have continued to generate controversy. Allegations regarding the use of pellet guns against protesters have circulated in connection with recent clashes. These allegations have not been independently verified or officially confirmed at the time of publication. 

While Wangchuk's decision to end his hunger strike has opened the door for dialogue between protest representatives and the Centre, organisers have reiterated that the movement will continue until their key demands are addressed. More official details are awaited as discussions progress.

title: TSG Bhasker Urges Administration to Act on Rising Prices and Shortage of Essential Commodities
author: Dweep Tulika
description: ANTCC leader TSG Bhasker urges the Andaman Administration to address rising prices and shortages of essential commodities across the Islands.
html:
Port Blair: Chairman of the Campaign Committee of the Andaman and Nicobar Pradesh Congress Committee (ANTCC), TSG Bhasker, has urged the Andaman and Nicobar Administration to take immediate steps to address what he described as a shortage and abnormal increase in the prices of essential commodities across the Islands.

In a letter addressed to the Director, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs, Bhasker said prices of several essential commodities had increased significantly over the past few months, placing an additional financial burden on consumers.

According to Bhasker, the increase has affected a wide range of items, including grains, sugar, cooking oil, vegetables, fruits, other perishable goods, medicines, household necessities and appliances.

Potato prices cited as example

Highlighting what he described as the severity of the situation, Bhasker said the price of potato had reportedly reached as high as ₹180 per kg.

He said such increases were particularly affecting middle-class and economically weaker families already facing a high cost of living in the Islands.

Call for examination of price rise

Bhasker urged the Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs Department to examine the reasons behind the reported increase in prices.

He suggested that the Administration assess whether the situation was linked to factors including supply shortages, transportation costs, distribution-related issues or other causes.

He also called for regular and adequate supplies of essential commodities across the Islands and urged the Administration to take measures to bring prices back to what he described as reasonable and affordable levels.

“The people of Andaman & Nicobar Islands should not be forced to bear the burden of unchecked price rise and shortages of basic necessities. The Administration must urgently intervene and ensure that essential commodities remain available at reasonable prices,” Bhasker said.

Editorial note: This report is based on the statement/letter issued by TSG Bhasker. The reported ₹180-per-kg potato price, the extent of shortages and the causes of price increases have not been independently verified in this report.

title: Little Andaman Hosts National-Level Surfing Championship at Butler Bay
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Little Andaman hosted the national-level Little Andaman Pro 2026 surfing championship at Butler Bay with surfers from across India.
html:
Port Blair, 18 Apr :

Little Andaman has recently hosted a national-level surfing competition, marking a notable development in India’s water sports landscape. The event, titled Little Andaman Pro 2026, was conducted at Butler Bay over a period of four days and saw participation from surfers representing different parts of the country.

In the main competition categories, Sivaraj Babu secured the top position in the men’s open division, while Kamali Moorthy emerged as the winner in the women’s open category. Kamali Moorthy also recorded the highest score of the event, making her performance one of the key highlights of the championship.

Apart from traditional surfing events, the competition also included Stand-Up Paddle (SUP) sprint races, expanding the scope of participation. In these events, Dinesh Selvamani won the men’s category, while Vijayalakshmi Irulappan secured the top position in the women’s category.

The championship featured a mix of experienced competitors and emerging surfers, indicating a gradual expansion of the sport’s talent base in India. Participants are understood to be preparing for higher-level competitions, including international events, reflecting a shift toward structured training and competitive exposure.

The event was supported by the Surfing Federation of India along with Andaman and Nicobar Tourism. Officials associated with the आयोजन indicated that such competitions are part of broader efforts to promote water sports activities in the islands and bring them into the national sporting framework.

Butler Bay in Little Andaman is considered suitable for surfing due to its consistent wave patterns, surf-friendly breaks, and relatively less crowded coastline. These natural conditions have contributed to its selection as a venue for national-level events.

The successful conduct of the championship highlights a growing focus on developing surfing as a sport in the region, qwhile also exploring its potential linkage with tourism and local economic activity.
