title: Candle March Held in Sri Vijaya Puram Against Proposed Deemed University Move
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Students and civil society members held a candle march in Sri Vijaya Puram against the proposed deemed university move.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram, 25 February 2026:

A candle march was held in Sri Vijaya Puram, South Andaman, protesting against the proposed move to convert the seven colleges of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, currently affiliated with Pondicherry University, into a deemed university system.

The march commenced from Flag Point and proceeded towards Tiranga Park, witnessing participation from students, civil society members, and representatives of various organisations.

During the public gathering at Tiranga Park, speakers associated with the Joint Action Forum (JAF), along with representatives from different political parties and social organisations, voiced concerns regarding the proposed decision.

Speakers argued that the move could negatively affect students’ access to quality higher education and urged authorities to reconsider the proposal in the interest of island students.

Participants carried candles as a symbol of peaceful resistance and unity, reflecting growing public concern over the future of higher education in the islands.

The programme concluded with appeals urging the administration and policymakers to review the decision while safeguarding the educational interests of students in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume VIII, Issue No. 12, dated 20 March 2026.

title: Dweep Tulika Public Opinion Survey 2026 | Share Your Voice, Shape Andaman's Future
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Participate in Dweep Tulika's Public Opinion Survey 2026 and share your views on the future of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
html:
CLICK HERE TO PARTICIPATE

📢 Andaman Speaks. Dweep Tulika Listens.

For the first time, Dweep Tulika is launching a month-long Public Opinion Survey to understand what the people of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands truly think.

🗓️ Survey Period: 21 July 2026 – 20 August 2026

Whether you're a student, homemaker, government employee, private employee, entrepreneur, fisherman, farmer, retired citizen, senior citizen—or anyone who calls these islands home—your opinion matters. There is no age restriction, and every resident of the islands is invited to participate.

We want to know:

✔️ What is working well in the islands?
✔️ What needs immediate attention?

title: MP Bishnu Pada Ray Raises Eight Pending Issues of Islanders with Union Home Minister Amit Shah
author: Dweep Tulika
description: MP Bishnu Pada Ray met Home Minister Amit Shah and submitted a memorandum seeking action on eight pending issues concerning Islanders.
html:
New Delhi | 10 August 2026

Member of Parliament from the Andaman & Nicobar Islands Shri Bishnu Pada Ray met Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah in New Delhi and submitted a memorandum seeking early resolution of eight issues concerning the Islanders.

According to the memorandum, the issues raised cover employment, higher education, development funding, local governance, rehabilitation, healthcare and the regularisation of long-serving workers.

A key demand was the introduction of a Domicile Law providing 100% job reservation for Islanders, along with an upper age limit of 40 years for Group-B (Non-Gazetted) and Group-C posts. The memorandum seeks such provisions on the lines of arrangements referred to by the MP in relation to the Union Territory of Ladakh. Ray has previously raised similar demands in Parliament.

The MP also sought the establishment of a Central University in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, replacing the existing deemed-university model. The demand for a Central University has previously been raised by Ray in Parliament.

On development funding, the memorandum called for an enhancement of the annual budget allocation for developmental works in the Islands.

Issues concerning Panchayati Raj Institutions and Municipal Councils were also raised. The MP sought adequate financial assistance for their functioning and development, along with restoration of their powers, functions and funds.

Regarding the Great Nicobar Island Project, the memorandum sought fair compensation and a suitable rehabilitation package for families affected by the project.

The MP further sought the upgradation of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands Institute of Medical Sciences (ANIIMS) into an AIIMS Centre, with the stated objective of improving access to advanced healthcare in the Islands. Ray has previously raised concerns regarding ANIIMS and healthcare infrastructure in Parliament and in representations to the Centre.

Another demand concerned casual, Daily Rated Mazdoor (DRM) and contractual employees who have been serving in various departments for several years. The memorandum sought a policy for their permanent absorption or regularisation. Ray has also raised the issue of regularisation of contractual workers in Parliament.

According to the memorandum, the Union Home Minister heard the issues raised by the MP and assured Shri Ray that the matters would be looked into for their early resolution.

The eight demands remain proposals placed before the Union Government and do not, by themselves, constitute government decisions or approvals.

title: MP Seeks Joint Inspection of Chatham Site for Ganesh, Durga Idol Immersion
author: Dweep Tulika
description: MP Bishnu Pada Ray seeks a joint inspection of the proposed Chatham site for Ganesh and Durga idol immersion ahead of the festival season.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 22, 2026

Member of Parliament for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Shri Bishnu Pada Ray, has requested the South Andaman District Administration to arrange a joint inspection of the proposed immersion site at Chatham for the upcoming Ganesh and Durga Puja idol immersions in Sri Vijaya Puram.

In a letter addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, South Andaman, the MP stated that representations had been received from various organisations and public representatives regarding arrangements for the forthcoming idol immersion ceremonies.

The letter notes that the traditional immersion site at Chatham Bridge is currently unavailable due to repair and maintenance works. It also highlights difficulties previously experienced at the alternative Junglighat/Marina area, including inadequate water depth during low tide, resurfacing of idols, traffic congestion and other logistical and environmental concerns.

Against this backdrop, Shri Ray has proposed that the New Vehicle Ferry Jetty/Solid Jetty at Chatham be considered as a designated immersion point, citing its reported water depth and accessibility for the movement of idols and accompanying vehicles.

The MP has requested a joint site inspection by the Port Management Board, District Administration, Police/Marine Police, Fire & Emergency Services, Disaster Management authorities and other concerned agencies, along with representatives of the Puja Committees.

The proposed inspection would help assess the suitability and safety of the location before a final decision is taken.

The letter also calls for arrangements relating to cleanliness, crowd and traffic management, and removal of debris following the immersion ceremonies.

With the festival season approaching, Shri Ray has urged the authorities to take up the matter on priority so that Puja Committees have sufficient time to make the necessary logistical arrangements.

title: Baby Goat Rescued from Tin Roof in Sundar Colony; Incident Raises Questions Over Livestock Responsibility
author: Dweep Tulika
description: A baby goat stranded on a tin rooftop in Sundar Colony was rescued by the Fire Service after a local resident raised the alarm.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | 3 August 2026

A baby goat that had reportedly remained stranded on a tin rooftop in Sundar Colony, Megapode, since the morning of 3 August was rescued at around 5 PM after the Fire Service was alerted by a local resident.

According to information received by Dweep Tulika, the Fire Service reached the location and completed the rescue within approximately half an hour of receiving the information.

A local resident, K Jyothi, an engineer, reportedly noticed the stranded animal and contacted the Fire Service, leading to its eventual rescue.

While the immediate incident ended safely, residents have raised concerns over what they describe as a recurring problem involving unattended goats and other livestock in the locality.

According to residents who spoke to Dweep Tulika, this was not the first such incident in the area. They recalled an earlier incident in which a goat reportedly fell into a well. Despite attempts by residents to rescue the animal, it was found too late and could not be saved.

The incidents have prompted questions about the responsibility of livestock owners to ensure that animals are safely contained and do not wander into hazardous locations.

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Municipal Regulation, 1994 provides municipalities with powers to regulate the keeping of animals and to make licensing provisions concerning premises used for keeping animals including sheep and goats.

At the same time, goat farming is an established livestock activity in the Islands. The Directorate of Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Services promotes goat farming and provides training and assistance to farmers.

The issue, therefore, is not the keeping of livestock itself, but whether animals are being properly contained, monitored and protected from avoidable risks in residential and municipal areas.

The use of emergency services for animal rescue also raises a question of prevention. While the Fire Service's intervention in this case helped prevent a potentially serious outcome, better supervision and appropriate containment by livestock owners could reduce the need for emergency intervention.

The incident also highlights the role of ordinary citizens in responding when animals are found in distress. In this case, a resident's decision to report the stranded goat ultimately led to its rescue.

For residents, the episode serves as a reminder that animal ownership carries a responsibility not only towards the animal but also towards the safety and convenience of the surrounding community.

Dweep Tulika could not independently verify the earlier reported goat incident or the frequency of similar cases in Sundar Colony. These details are based on information provided by local residents.

title: MaaSanskriti Seeks to Bridge the Gap Between Talent and Opportunity
author: Dweep Tulika
description: MaaSanskriti Society is a community-focused initiative seeking to connect talent, ideas and aspirations with people, platforms and opportunities.
html:
Sri Vijayapuram:

Talent can exist across communities, but access to platforms, networks and resources that help individuals develop that talent is not always equally available. Against this backdrop, MaaSanskriti Society presents itself as a community-focused initiative seeking to connect people with talent, ideas and aspirations to opportunities and resources that can support their growth.

The concept is centred around bringing together a diverse group of people, including students, artists, creators, entrepreneurs, professionals and other community members, with the aim of encouraging connections, learning and collaboration.

At the core of MaaSanskriti's vision is the idea of acting as a bridge between individuals with talent and potential and the organisations, mentors, institutions, businesses and resources that may help them move forward.

The initiative's broader approach is to encourage communities to become active participants in creating connections and opportunities rather than simply waiting for opportunities to emerge.

For the islands, where individuals with skills and creative or entrepreneurial ideas may sometimes have limited access to wider professional networks and platforms, the concept could provide an avenue for greater visibility, collaboration and exchange.

MaaSanskriti's message can be summed up in three objectives: discover talent, connect people and create opportunities.

title: Investigation Ordered Against AATO by South Andaman Administration
author: Dweep Tulika
description: South Andaman Administration has ordered an inquiry into AATO, seeking records related to governance, finances and compliance.
html:
Port Blair, April 2026:

The office of the Deputy Commissioner, South Andaman, has issued an official investigation notice to the Andaman Association of Tour Operators (AATO), seeking detailed records and documentation related to its functioning and financial transactions. The notice, issued by the Assistant Commissioner of South Andaman, marks the beginning of a formal administrative inquiry into the association.

According to the official communication, the association has been directed to produce a comprehensive set of documents, including certified meeting minutes of governing body sessions, original bye-laws along with any amendments, and updated records of office bearers.

The administration has also sought detailed accounting records such as cash books, transaction summaries, and audited statements to examine financial transparency and compliance with regulatory norms.

The notice further calls for documentation related to institutional grants, expenditure proofs, and banking details, including account-related records and KYC documents. Specific financial transactions mentioned in the notice are also under scrutiny, indicating a focused examination of certain monetary dealings involving the association.

Officials have stated that the inquiry is part of an ongoing administrative process aimed at verifying adherence to prescribed rules and ensuring transparency in the functioning of registered bodies.

The association has been instructed to submit the required documents within a stipulated timeframe, failing which further action may be considered.

Sources indicate that the matter may have wider implications for governance and regulatory oversight of registered associations in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The administration is expected to review the submitted records before determining the next course of action in the inquiry.

title: Andaman Police Warns Public Against Unauthorized UPI Auto-Payments
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Andaman Police issued an advisory warning citizens about unauthorized UPI auto-payments and recurring bank deductions.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram, 15 March 2026:

The Andaman and Nicobar Police has issued a public advisory warning citizens about unauthorized UPI auto-payments that may result in recurring deductions from bank accounts without users being fully aware.

According to the advisory, many users unknowingly approve UPI mandates or auto-debit instructions while subscribing to online services or completing digital transactions.

Officials stated that such mandates can lead to repeated monthly deductions if users fail to regularly monitor their active payment permissions.

The police have urged citizens to review and manage their UPI mandates through the official portal of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

Steps Suggested by Police:

  • Visit: upihelp.npci.org.in
  • Verify your bank-linked mobile number using OTP
  • Review all active UPI mandates
  • Revoke any mandate you do not recognize

Authorities also advised users not to approve unknown payment requests and to regularly check bank account activity to avoid fraud or unauthorized deductions.

In case of cyber fraud, citizens can contact the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or report incidents through the official portal: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal

The advisory highlights increasing concerns over digital payment security and the importance of public awareness regarding online financial safety.

title: Raghav Chadha Questions ‘28-Day Monthly Recharge Plans’ in Parliament
author: Dweep Tulika
description: AAP MP Raghav Chadha raised concerns in Parliament over telecom companies offering 28-day “monthly” recharge plans.
html:
New Delhi, 11 March 2026:

Raghav Chadha has raised concerns in Parliament regarding telecom companies’ so-called “monthly” prepaid recharge plans, questioning their transparency and fairness towards consumers.

Speaking on the issue, Chadha pointed out that many telecom recharge plans marketed as monthly actually provide validity for only 28 days instead of a full calendar month.

He argued that this system forces consumers to recharge 13 times in a year rather than 12, effectively increasing their annual expenditure.

Explaining the calculation, Chadha noted that 28 days multiplied by 13 recharges amounts to 364 days, resulting in users paying for an additional recharge every year.

The issue has triggered wider discussions on consumer rights, transparency in telecom pricing, and the need for clearer communication from service providers.

Chadha further stated that if telecom companies market plans as “monthly,” they should follow the actual calendar month system to ensure fairness for consumers.

title: Great Nicobar Project: India’s Mega Strategic Development Plan in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Overview of the Great Nicobar Project, its strategic purpose, infrastructure plans and environmental concerns.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram, May 30:

The proposed Great Nicobar Island Development Project has emerged as one of the largest infrastructure and strategic development initiatives planned in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in recent decades.

The project aims to transform Great Nicobar Island into a major maritime, aviation, logistics and strategic hub due to its proximity to the Strait of Malacca — one of the busiest international shipping routes in the world.

The idea of developing Great Nicobar for strategic purposes has existed for several decades, with the island repeatedly identified as an important location for India’s maritime and defence interests in the Indian Ocean region.

In recent years, the Government of India accelerated planning efforts under a broader Indo-Pacific strategy focusing on economic growth, maritime strength and regional connectivity.

According to official plans, the project includes four major components:

  1. An International Container Transshipment Terminal at Galathea Bay,
  2. A Greenfield International Airport for civilian and military use,
  3. A power generation facility,
  4. And a modern township with supporting infrastructure.

Government agencies have stated that the proposed transshipment terminal is intended to reduce India’s dependence on foreign ports such as Singapore, Colombo and Port Klang for cargo movement and international trade handling.

The project has been associated with several agencies including NITI Aayog, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation and various ministries related to shipping, defence, infrastructure and environment.

The modern phase of the project gained momentum between 2018 and 2020 when planning studies and feasibility assessments were initiated. Environmental assessment procedures formally began in 2021, followed by environmental and forest clearances during 2022.

Supporters of the project describe it as a major opportunity for economic growth, employment generation, tourism, trade expansion and national security enhancement.

However, the proposal has also attracted criticism and environmental concerns from researchers, activists and tribal rights groups.

Concerns raised include possible biodiversity loss, impact on rainforest ecosystems, effects on endangered leatherback turtle nesting sites and potential risks to indigenous communities including the Shompen tribe.

Questions have also been raised regarding large-scale tree felling and the island’s vulnerability to earthquakes and tsunamis following the 2004 Indian Ocean disaster.

According to recent official updates, planning and preparatory activities related to the project continue under government supervision, with authorities describing the initiative as strategically important for India’s long-term maritime and economic interests.

This report is based on publicly available government statements, planning documents, environmental reports and media coverage.

title: Indian Navy Commissions Three Indigenous Naval Platforms: INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak and INS Agray
author: Dweep Tulika
description: PM Modi commissioned INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak and INS Agray, boosting India's indigenous naval capabilities.
html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi commissioned three indigenously designed and built naval platforms in Kolkata, strengthening India's maritime capabilities and defence self-reliance.

Kolkata, June 21:

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday commissioned three indigenously designed and built naval platforms  INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak and INS Agray at a ceremony held in Kolkata.

The induction of the three vessels marks a significant milestone in India's efforts to strengthen maritime security and advance the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat through indigenous defence manufacturing.

INS Dunagiri is an advanced stealth frigate equipped with modern surveillance systems, sensors and weapon platforms designed to enhance the Indian Navy's operational capabilities across multiple mission profiles.

INS Sanshodhak is a modern survey vessel intended for hydrographic and oceanographic operations. The platform will support navigational safety, maritime mapping and scientific studies in Indian waters.

INS Agray is an anti-submarine warfare vessel developed to detect, track and counter underwater threats in coastal and near-shore environments, contributing to maritime security and naval preparedness.

Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Modi said the commissioning of the three platforms reflects India's growing defence capabilities and increasing self-reliance in strategic sectors.

He emphasized that maritime strength plays a vital role in enhancing a nation's economic influence, trade security and strategic reach.

According to official information, the three vessels were designed and constructed in India with a high percentage of indigenous components, showcasing the country's progress in shipbuilding, defence technology and domestic industrial capability.

The induction of the platforms is expected to enhance the Indian Navy's operational readiness across combat operations, hydrographic surveys and anti-submarine warfare missions.

The commissioning also highlights India's continued focus on strengthening maritime infrastructure and reducing dependence on foreign defence imports through indigenous innovation and manufacturing.

title: TPO Ban: What the UK and EU Restrictions Mean for India
author: Dweep Tulika
description: UK and EU restrictions on TPO in cosmetics raise questions for India, where no comparable blanket ban on TPO has been identified.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 24, 2026

The United Kingdom has introduced restrictions on cosmetics containing Trimethylbenzoyl Diphenylphosphine Oxide (TPO), a photoinitiator commonly used in UV- and LED-cured gel nail products. The move follows the European Union, which prohibited TPO in cosmetics from September 2025 after its classification as a Category 1B reproductive toxicant.

The restrictions have raised questions among nail professionals and consumers in India, where TPO-containing gel polishes and related products continue to be available.

The UK restrictions do not ban gel manicures or UV/LED nail products as a category. Instead, they concern cosmetic products containing TPO. Existing stocks are also subject to transitional provisions under the UK's regulatory framework.

In India, however, there is currently no evidence of a comparable blanket ban specifically prohibiting TPO in cosmetics. India's cosmetic products are regulated under the Cosmetics Rules, 2020, administered through the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The difference in regulatory approaches means that a product restricted or prohibited in the EU or UK may still be available in the Indian market. This does not automatically mean that such products are illegal in India, but it highlights the importance of checking their ingredients and regulatory compliance.

For consumers using gel nail products, the development also raises a broader question: Should India review its position on TPO in light of the regulatory action taken by the EU and UK?

Until any specific Indian regulatory notification is issued, claims that “TPO is banned in India” would be misleading.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

title: Kiren Rijiju Highlights Vision for Developed Andaman & Nicobar, Backs Great Nicobar Project
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju outlined Vision 2047 for Andaman & Nicobar and defended the proposed Great Nicobar Project.
html:
Union Minister Kiren Rijiju has said that the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are no longer a remote region and are set to play an important role in India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Addressing a gathering comprising professionals, business leaders, senior citizens, women, youth and BJP leaders during his visit to the islands, Rijiju emphasized the importance of direct interaction between policymakers and society. He noted that while digital communication has become widespread, face-to-face engagement remains essential for understanding local concerns and strengthening public participation.

Speaking about the transformation of remote regions, Rijiju said areas such as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Northeast and border regions were once viewed as distant from the country's mainstream development process. According to him, improved transportation, internet connectivity and digital infrastructure have significantly changed that perception over the past decade.

The minister highlighted initiatives such as Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar integration and digital payment systems, stating that these reforms have improved financial inclusion and enabled welfare benefits to reach beneficiaries directly.

Referring to India's economic progress, Rijiju said the country has emerged as one of the world's fastest-growing major economies and is working towards the goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047, the centenary year of India's independence.

He also discussed global economic and geopolitical challenges, including developments in West Asia and their impact on energy markets. According to him, the government has taken measures to reduce the burden of such challenges on ordinary citizens.

During his address, Rijiju criticized opposition parties, particularly the Congress, alleging that previous governments lacked a clear long-term development vision and did not adequately integrate remote regions into the national growth framework.

A significant portion of the minister's speech focused on the proposed Great Nicobar development project. Rijiju strongly defended the initiative, describing it as a strategic project aimed at strengthening national security, boosting economic activity and creating future opportunities for the islands.

He stated that the project had undergone extensive consultations and scientific assessments and argued that environmental conservation and development can coexist when supported by appropriate safeguards and responsible planning.

The minister also criticized groups opposing the project, alleging that some were attempting to obstruct development through misleading narratives. He maintained that the government's objective is to balance environmental protection with economic growth.

Highlighting the strategic importance of the islands, Rijiju said Andaman and Nicobar possesses immense potential due to its biodiversity, marine resources and location in the Bay of Bengal. He expressed confidence that the islands could emerge as a globally recognised destination for tourism, investment and sustainable development.

Emphasizing responsible tourism, he called for efforts to attract high-value visitors while preserving the islands' ecological balance and natural beauty. He also urged local residents and businesses to contribute towards environmental protection and cleanliness.

Concluding his address, Rijiju appealed to intellectuals, professionals, community leaders, women, youth and senior citizens to actively participate in the development journey of the islands, stating that the goal is to build a developed India and a developed Andaman and Nicobar for future generations.

title: AK-47 Firing During Student Protest in Bihar Triggers Political Row
author: Dweep Tulika
description: A Bihar Police constable has been suspended after firing an AK-47 during student protests in Siwan, triggering political debate over police conduct.
html:
Siwan, Bihar | 29 July 2026

The ongoing nationwide student agitation over the alleged NEET examination paper leak has intensified after a Bihar Police constable was suspended for firing an AK-47 rifle during protests in Siwan, an incident captured in widely circulated videos that has sparked political controversy and renewed scrutiny of police conduct.

The protests began over allegations of irregularities in the NEET examination and later expanded to include broader concerns relating to youth unemployment, accountability and education reforms. Demonstrations have continued across several states despite recent political developments.

During the Bihar Bandh on 25 July, videos showed a police constable running towards protesters while carrying an AK-47 rifle and firing several rounds into the air. Bihar Police confirmed that the weapon was discharged without authorisation, suspended the constable with immediate effect and initiated departmental proceedings. Senior police officials stated that the use of the assault rifle could not be justified and that the officer acted without orders.

The incident has triggered heated political reactions, with opposition leaders demanding an independent investigation into the use of force during the protests and accountability for those responsible. Government representatives have defended the disciplinary action against the constable, while broader political debate over the handling of the demonstrations continues.

The AK-47 firing has emerged as one of the defining images of the ongoing student movement, reigniting discussions over policing standards during public protests and the balance between maintaining law and order and safeguarding citizens' constitutional right to peaceful assembly. Investigations into the incident remain underway.

title: TSG Charitable Foundation Donates Smart TV to Government Primary School in Car Nicobar
author: Dweep Tulika
description: TSG Charitable Foundation donated a Smart TV to Government Primary School, Kinyuka, Car Nicobar, during a Smart Classroom inauguration.
html:
Car Nicobar | 7 August 2026

The TSG Charitable Foundation donated a Smart TV to the Government Primary School at Kinyuka, Car Nicobar, as part of a Smart Classroom initiative, according to information provided regarding the programme.

The Smart TV was handed over by Shri TSG Bhasker, Chairman of TSG Charitable Foundation, during the inauguration of the Smart Classroom on 7 August.

The initiative is aimed at expanding access to digital learning resources for students in the remote island region. The introduction of Smart Classroom facilities is expected to provide teachers with additional tools for classroom instruction and give students greater exposure to digital educational content.

The school serves children from the Nicobarese community, and the initiative is intended to support access to modern educational resources in the island setting.

According to the information provided by the organisers, the school management, teachers and parents expressed appreciation for the contribution and said that access to digital learning resources would support students' educational development.

The contribution adds a digital-learning component to the school's classroom infrastructure, although the long-term impact will depend on factors including reliable electricity, connectivity, availability of educational content and continued technical support.

The initiative also highlights the role that community and charitable organisations can play in supplementing educational infrastructure in remote island communities.

title: Census Appointments Renew Debate Over Workforce Planning in Andaman & Nicobar
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Recent census appointments in Andaman and Nicobar Islands have renewed debate over workforce planning and repeated deployment of staff.
html:
Sri Vijayapuram, April 10, 2026:

The recent appointment of government personnel for census duties in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands has renewed discussion over administrative planning and workforce utilisation, drawing attention to a governance practice that has increasingly come under public scrutiny.

While the move is legally supported under the Census Act, 1948, which authorises the deployment of government staff for national exercises, concerns are being raised regarding the repeated reliance on the same categories of employees for multiple administrative responsibilities.

In regions such as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where manpower availability remains limited, teachers, health workers and administrative personnel are frequently assigned duties beyond their primary roles. From census operations to election work and public health campaigns, repeated deployment has gradually become an established administrative pattern.

Observers argue that while the approach may offer short-term administrative convenience, it also highlights the absence of a dedicated auxiliary workforce capable of supporting large-scale national exercises. Departments more closely aligned with field data collection, including statistical and revenue units, are often perceived as comparatively underutilised.

Experts suggest that teachers and similar personnel are commonly selected because of their literacy, organisational reliability and ease of mobilisation. However, the practice has raised concerns regarding its broader institutional impact.

The diversion of teachers can affect classroom continuity, particularly in smaller island regions where substitute arrangements remain limited. Similarly, assigning non-medical responsibilities to healthcare personnel may place additional strain on already stretched public health systems.

The issue has also reopened broader discussions regarding fairness and equitable workload distribution within government departments, with some observers linking the debate to constitutional principles of equality and administrative balance.

At the same time, concerns over manpower shortages continue to exist despite a section of educated youth in the islands reportedly remaining underutilised due to limited employment opportunities.

Experts have suggested that structured engagement of trained youth in temporary national exercises such as census operations could reduce pressure on existing government staff while improving efficiency through more role-specific deployment. At present, however, no formal mechanism exists to systematically integrate such a workforce into administrative processes.

Census operations play a critical role in national planning, influencing decisions related to welfare schemes, infrastructure development and public resource allocation. As a result, questions regarding data accuracy and operational consistency have also emerged.

Although short-term training programmes are conducted prior to field deployment, some experts believe that assigning large-scale data collection responsibilities to personnel without specialised experience may affect consistency in data gathering across diverse regions and conditions.

The issue carries particular significance in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where geographic isolation and limited institutional capacity often magnify the impact of administrative inefficiencies. In such conditions, diversion of personnel can affect the functioning of entire departments with limited scope for replacement or operational backup.

While the legal framework continues to support such appointments, evolving administrative demands have intensified calls for a broader re-evaluation of workforce planning strategies.

The debate surrounding census appointments increasingly reflects a larger governance question—not merely whether authorities possess the power to deploy personnel, but whether existing systems represent the most efficient and equitable utilisation of available human resources.

As discussions continue, many observers believe that improved workforce planning, broader participation and more specialised role allocation could significantly strengthen administrative outcomes, particularly in geographically sensitive regions such as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume IX, Issue No. 1.

title: Greta Thunberg Joins SFI UK Demonstration in Support of Indian Student Movement
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Greta Thunberg joined an SFI UK demonstration in London expressing solidarity with the Indian student movement and calling for international support.
html:
London | 29 July 2026

Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg joined a demonstration organised by the Students' Federation of India (SFI) UK in London to express solidarity with the recent student movement in India. The event brought together members of the Indian diaspora, students and supporters to voice support for the campaign.

Addressing the gathering, Thunberg praised the Indian students' movement, describing it as a source of hope and an example of the power of collective action. She said the students' struggle for justice and democracy deserved international solidarity and support.

The demonstration was organised by the SFI's United Kingdom unit and followed recent developments in India's student movement. According to the organisers, the event reflected growing international attention towards the issues raised by student protesters in India.

Greta Thunberg is internationally recognised for her climate activism and has addressed several global forums, including the United Nations Climate Action Summit, on issues relating to climate change and environmental justice.

SFI UK members also indicated that they hope to engage with international environmental advocates in the future on issues affecting India, including environmental concerns surrounding the Great Nicobar Infrastructure (GNI) Project. However, there has been no public confirmation from Greta Thunberg regarding any future campaign or involvement related to the project.

title: Andaman & Nicobar Rowers Win Three Medals at Sub-Junior National Championship
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Andaman & Nicobar rowers won one silver and two bronze medals at the 27th Sub-Junior National Rowing Championship in Kolkata.
html:
Kolkata | 9 August 2026

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands rowing team secured three medals at the 27th Sub-Junior National Rowing Championship 2026, held at Rabindra Sarobar Lake in Kolkata, West Bengal.

The championship was held from 5 to 9 August 2026 and was organised by the Rowing Federation of India. The Andaman & Nicobar Rowing Association had conducted selection trials in July to choose the Islands' team for the national championship.

According to the results provided to Dweep Tulika, Carelyne and Sunidhi won a Silver Medal in the YJG2X category.

In the SJG2 category, Zeeya Victor and Anu secured a Bronze Medal. Another Bronze Medal was won by Sanvi, Anita, Suzun and Lenity in the SJG4 category.

The three-medal haul included one silver and two bronze medals across different events.

The performances represent a notable achievement for the young rowers from the Islands, particularly given the geographical challenges involved in accessing mainland sporting competitions and training opportunities.

Shri G. Bhasker, President of the Andaman & Nicobar Rowing Association, along with committee members, congratulated the medal-winning athletes and their coaches for their performances. The association appreciated the rowers' commitment and hard work and conveyed its best wishes for their future competitions.

The achievement adds to the growing participation of young athletes from the Islands in national-level sporting events.

Source: Information provided by the Andaman & Nicobar Rowing Association.


Verification note: The championship venue and dates were independently corroborated; independent verification of the three specific 2026 medal results was not established from the publicly accessible official results at the time of publication.

title: Rakhigarhi Human Remains Sent for Advanced Scientific Study to Unlock Harappan Secrets
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Human skeletal remains from Rakhigarhi have been transferred for advanced DNA and anthropological research.
html:
Human skeletal remains excavated from Rakhigarhi, the largest known settlement of the Indus-Saraswati Civilization, have been transferred for advanced scientific analysis.

New Delhi, June 22:

Human skeletal remains excavated from the archaeological site of Rakhigarhi in Haryana have been transferred by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to the Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI) for detailed scientific investigation.

Rakhigarhi, spread across nearly 550 hectares, is regarded as the largest known settlement of the Indus-Saraswati Civilization and one of the most important archaeological sites in South Asia.

During excavations carried out in the 2025-26 field season, archaeologists uncovered eight burials at a cemetery site within the ancient settlement. Three complete human skeletons along with skeletal fragments have now been moved to AnSI's specialised laboratory in Kolkata for advanced research.

Scientists plan to use modern techniques including ancient DNA (aDNA) analysis, isotope studies, osteological examinations and palaeopathological investigations to better understand the lives of the Harappan people.

Researchers hope the studies will provide valuable insights into ancestry, migration patterns, diet, disease, health conditions and environmental adaptation during the Harappan period more than 4,000 years ago.

The project will involve collaboration with leading institutions including the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), Banaras Hindu University (BHU), University College London (UCL) and other scientific organisations.

Experts believe the findings could significantly improve understanding of the origins, biological history and population movements associated with one of the world's earliest urban civilizations.

Officials said the initiative also marks a renewed effort to strengthen India's palaeoanthropological and ancient DNA research capabilities through cooperation between archaeology, anthropology and genetics.

title: Jobs, Roads, Healthcare and Islanders’ Rights: ANDC Leaders Raise Key Concerns Ahead of 2027 Elections
author: Dweep Tulika
description: ANDC leaders PK Halder and Manoj Paul discuss job reservation, healthcare, roads, cargo connectivity, tourism and Islanders’ rights ahead of 2027 elec
html:
PK Halder and Manoj Paul outline positions on local employment, healthcare, connectivity, tourism, economic opportunities and greater powers for Panchayati Raj institutions

Sri Vijayapuram, 06 Sep 2026:

Employment, healthcare, connectivity, rising costs and what the party describes as the “first right” of Islanders over jobs, land and economic opportunities emerged as major themes in a wide-ranging discussion with Andaman Nicobar Democratic Congress (ANDC) leaders Paritosh Kumar Halder (PK Halder) and Manoj Paul.

The discussion, conducted by the Chief Editor of Dweep Tulika, covered issues ranging from 100% job reservation and recruitment to healthcare facilities in remote islands, road connectivity, cargo costs, tourism and the powers of Panchayati Raj institutions.

100% job reservation remains a central demand

PK Halder said the principal objective of the ANDC is to ensure that Islanders receive the maximum benefit from employment and development opportunities.

He argued that non-gazetted government posts should receive priority for Islanders, pointing to arrangements in other parts of the country where local candidates receive preferential access to employment.

Halder also referred to Ladakh, arguing that if similar provisions for local employment can exist there, Islanders should also be able to secure stronger employment protection.

He said unemployment among local youth remains a major concern and referred to a commitment he attributed to BJP national president J.P. Nadda regarding 100% job reservation, which he said had not materialised.

Concerns over recruitment of non-Islanders

Halder alleged that more than half of some recent appointments had gone to non-Islanders, describing the situation as a serious concern for local job seekers.

He called for greater scrutiny of recruitment and greater involvement of the Lieutenant Governor and the Central Government in addressing the issue.

Halder said the Union Territory's position under the Union Government, particularly under the administrative framework involving the Home Ministry, provides an opportunity to create a specific mechanism for Islanders.

One possible solution, he suggested, would be legislation or an administrative framework establishing a permanent residential qualification for non-gazetted posts, with such employment reserved for Islanders.

Manoj Paul links employment to the wider economy

Manoj Paul connected the employment issue with the broader economic participation of Islanders.

He argued that when people from outside the Islands obtain jobs or economic opportunities locally, the benefits do not necessarily remain within the local population. He also discussed taxation and GST while making the case for greater economic opportunities for Islanders.

Paul said the question should not be limited to government employment, but should also include who receives opportunities to operate businesses and participate in the local economy.

“First right” over business and resources

Paul argued that Islanders should have what he described as the “first right” over the Islands' resources, employment and business opportunities.

Drawing comparisons with states and regions where local populations receive preferential access to employment or economic opportunities, he said the same principle should apply in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

He also raised concerns about people from outside purchasing land and establishing businesses in the Islands, arguing that stronger safeguards were needed to protect Islanders' long-term interests.

The broader argument, he said, was about what the present generation would leave behind for future generations.

Healthcare remains a major concern

Healthcare emerged as another major issue during the discussion.

Halder highlighted the situation in Little Andaman, where he said residents face shortages of specialised medical facilities. He pointed to difficulties faced by pregnant women and the need for some patients to travel to Port Blair for treatment.

He argued that remote islands should have essential medical facilities, including diagnostic services, laboratory facilities and specialist doctors.

Paul also raised concerns about government hospitals, claiming that some facilities lacked medicines, functioning diagnostic equipment and adequate technical staff.

These claims represent the assessments of the speakers and would require independent verification before being presented as established deficiencies.

Roads, electricity and water

Both speakers placed basic infrastructure at the centre of their development concerns.

The discussion highlighted poor roads, electricity shortages and water-supply problems, particularly in remote areas.

Halder argued that development cannot be meaningful if Islanders lack reliable roads, hospitals, schools, water and electricity.

He also criticised what he described as inadequate accountability when infrastructure projects fail to deliver results, advocating a stronger “reward and punishment” mechanism for officials responsible for public projects.

Panchayati Raj institutions need greater powers

Halder also advocated greater administrative and financial powers for Panchayati Raj institutions.

He argued that elected representatives at the Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and District Council levels currently have insufficient authority to independently undertake development work.

According to Halder, excessive administrative restrictions have weakened local institutions and prevented Panchayats from responding effectively to village-level requirements.

He said Panchayats should instead be empowered, while corruption should be addressed through accountability and punishment rather than restricting the institution as a whole.

North and Middle Andaman: inflation and cargo connectivity

Paul identified rising prices as one of the major issues affecting North and Middle Andaman.

He argued that inadequate direct cargo unloading and shipping connectivity contribute to higher costs for essential goods and construction materials in the region.

According to Paul, improved cargo connectivity could benefit not only consumers but also truck operators, small businesses, transport workers and other local economic activities.

He argued that a better cargo network could create a wider local “business cycle” and contribute to tourism and economic growth.

Government ships and transport costs

Both ANDC leaders also discussed the role of government and private operators in transport.

Paul argued that government and private operators should both be allowed to function so that private monopolies do not emerge in shipping and transport.

Halder supported greater government participation, saying government-operated ships could help bring down cargo and freight costs while providing competition to private operators.

Paul extended the argument to airfares, suggesting that government intervention could be considered where fares become excessive.

Three priorities if elected to Parliament

When asked by the Dweep Tulika Chief Editor about the party's priorities if elected to Parliament, Manoj Paul listed three broad areas:

  1. 100% job reservation for Islanders
  2. Opening Andaman tourism to the world
  3. Addressing population-related concerns through a proposed cut-off/inner-line framework

On tourism, Paul argued that the Islands require better connectivity and wider access to international and domestic visitors.

On population, he proposed a system involving a cut-off date for people arriving after 2010, along with restrictions relating to settlement and land rights.

The proposal is a political position put forward by Paul and is not presented as an existing policy.

A politics centred on Islanders' development

The discussion repeatedly returned to the argument that political choices should be based on the long-term interests of Islanders rather than short-term electoral considerations.

Paul rejected religious and caste-based politics, saying the party's focus should instead be on the development of Islanders across communities.

For the ANDC leaders, jobs, healthcare, roads, transport, tourism, land and local economic opportunities are interconnected issues.

Their message ahead of the 2027 elections is that development policies should place the interests of Islanders at the centre of governance, while strengthening local institutions and improving accountability.

Editorial Note: The allegations, figures, comparisons, political assessments and proposed policy measures in this report are attributed to PK Halder and Manoj Paul. Dweep Tulika has not independently established claims made by the speakers unless specifically stated otherwise.

title: About the Editor-in-Chief, Dweep Tulika News
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Learn about R. Vineeth, Editor-in-Chief of Dweep Tulika, former Indian Air Force personnel, journalist, mountaineer and public affairs commentator fro
html:
R. Vineeth

Editor-in-Chief, Dweep Tulika

R. Vineeth is the Editor-in-Chief of Dweep Tulika, one of the oldest Bengali newspapers published from the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. He is a journalist committed to factual, independent and public-interest journalism, with a focus on governance, public policy, strategic affairs, environment, culture and issues affecting island communities.

A former member of the Indian Air Force, Vineeth brings experience gained from disciplined operational environments to his work in journalism. His reporting is shaped by field exposure, resilience and a practical understanding of the challenges associated with remote island administration and public service.

Based in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, he has been actively involved in regional journalism, public affairs and cultural documentation, working to highlight issues that often receive limited national attention. His editorial approach combines verified reporting with in-depth analysis, ensuring that local developments are presented within their broader social, economic and strategic context.

Beyond journalism, Vineeth maintains a long-standing association with mountaineering, trekking and adventure activities, experiences that have strengthened his appreciation of the islands' geography, environment and diverse communities.

Under his editorial leadership, Dweep Tulika continues to document the evolving story of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands through responsible journalism, historical preservation and community engagement, while covering national and international developments that impact the region.

  • Strategic & Defence Affairs
  • Maritime Security
  • Environment & Biodiversity
  • Indigenous Communities

title: Andaman Flight Crisis: Tourism Stakeholders Announce Further Action After Protest
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Tourism stakeholders in Andaman announce further action after protest, seeking more flights and affordable airfares through meetings with authorities
html:
Delegations plan meetings with the MP, Lieutenant Governor and Union Civil Aviation Minister as stakeholders seek increased flight frequency and affordable airfares.

Andaman Flight Crisis: Tourism Stakeholders Announce Further Action After Protest

Port Blair: A day after a protest over reduced flight frequency and rising airfares affecting the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, representatives of tourism and allied sectors held a press briefing at TSG Emerald View, outlining their follow-up plans and calling for continued action to address the island's air connectivity concerns.

The representatives said that following the protest, they met the Director of the Airports Authority of India, the Secretary of Civil Aviation in the Andaman & Nicobar Administration and the Chief Secretary.

According to the speakers, the response from the officials was positive, with the issue being discussed as one extending beyond tourism and affecting several sections of the island economy.

The stakeholders said the flight situation is affecting not only tourism operators but also fishermen, auto and cab drivers, tour operators, private agents and other businesses dependent on the movement of tourists and goods.

They described the issue as having two broad dimensions—supporting the tourism industry and addressing the wider connectivity and infrastructure requirements of Islanders.

Proposal for Subsidised Air Travel

One of the proposals discussed during the meetings was the possibility of making around 25 seats on a flight available at subsidised fares.

The representatives argued that high airfares have made air travel increasingly difficult for both Islanders and visitors.

During the briefing, one speaker cited a figure of ₹77,000 as a subsidy for a single ticket, describing it as information received during the meeting.

The stakeholders questioned whether such expenditure could instead be utilised to make a limited number of airline seats available at more affordable fares for Islanders.

They suggested that a suitable subsidy mechanism could potentially enable some seats to be offered at substantially reduced prices.

The speakers also said that airfares to destinations including Chennai, Kolkata and Delhi had shown some reduction following the protest and argued that continued engagement could result in further relief.

The subsidy figure and airfare changes cited during the briefing were statements made by the participants and have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

Three-Pronged Follow-Up Plan

The forum said the protest would not be treated as a one-day campaign.

According to the announcement, the next phase will include a delegation meeting the Member of Parliament, seeking an appointment with the Lieutenant Governor, and sending a delegation to Delhi to seek a meeting with the Union Civil Aviation Minister.

The proposed Delhi delegation will present the stakeholders' concerns and seek intervention regarding flight connectivity and airfares in the islands.

The representatives also thanked the Chamber of Commerce for submitting its own representation and acknowledged the participation of tourism stakeholders and Islanders in the protest.

Fisheries Sector Raises Concerns

A representative of the fisheries sector highlighted the impact of reduced flight services on the movement of fish.

He said the reduction in flights had affected the sector's ability to transport fish and claimed that the islands had previously been exporting approximately 20 tonnes of fish per day.

He also referred to losses resulting from delays in packing and transporting the produce, saying the situation was affecting employment and the wider fisheries economy.

The representative called for increased flight frequency and lower fares, arguing that improved connectivity would also contribute to the revival of tourist arrivals and benefit hotels and other tourism-dependent businesses.

The figure of 20 tonnes per day was cited by the speaker during the briefing and has not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

Tourism Industry Seeks Advance Planning

Another speaker thanked Islanders and tourism stakeholders for participating in the previous day's protest and said the campaign was aimed at protecting the tourism industry.

According to the speaker, the reduction in flights since around mid-May had contributed to difficulties for tourism-related businesses.

He stressed the need to prepare in advance for the next tourism season rather than waiting until the connectivity situation becomes more difficult.

Describing tourism as a major contributor to the island economy, he said stakeholders would continue working together and thanked those who helped mobilise support through WhatsApp groups and other channels.

The speaker also thanked the media for highlighting the concerns and bringing them to a wider audience.

Cab Operators Warn of Wider Economic Impact

The tourist transport sector also raised concerns during the briefing.

A representative said tourist transport operators form an important part of the tourism ecosystem and claimed that a substantial proportion of tourist cab operators were facing financial difficulties, including liabilities under various schemes.

He said losses that may appear relatively small at the individual operator level can become a much larger economic problem when considered across the sector.

The representative appealed to those who were unable to participate in the previous day's protest because of other commitments to support future actions.

He said correspondence with the authorities would continue and that stakeholders would be kept informed about further developments.

“The Forum Will Continue Until a Conclusion”

The representatives indicated that further administrative representations and public engagement would continue until what they described as a definite conclusion is reached.

They appealed to Islanders, the Administration and the concerned ministry to support efforts to address the difficulties being faced by the island economy.

The stakeholders also thanked the media for helping bring the issue to wider public attention.

The press briefing therefore marked a transition from the initial protest to a sustained campaign involving administrative meetings, political representations and a proposed delegation to Delhi.

For the stakeholders, the immediate demands remain increased flight frequency and affordable airfares.

The broader concern, however, extends beyond tourism to fisheries, transportation, employment, trade and other parts of the island economy that depend on reliable air connectivity.

The next significant developments are expected to follow the proposed meetings with the Member of Parliament, Lieutenant Governor and Union Civil Aviation Minister.

Editorial Note: This report is based on statements made by tourism and allied-sector representatives during the press briefing at TSG Emerald View. Figures, claims and assessments attributed to individual speakers have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika unless otherwise stated.

title: Students Protest Teacher Shortage at PM SHRI School in Rajasthan's Jalore
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Students at PM SHRI Government Senior Secondary School in Mengalwa, Jalore, protested over an alleged shortage of teachers, demanding regular appointm
html:
Jalore, Rajasthan | 29 July 2026

Students of PM SHRI Government Senior Secondary School, Mengalwa, in Rajasthan's Jalore district staged a protest over an alleged shortage of teaching staff, arguing that regular classes could not function effectively without adequate teachers.

According to reports, the students locked the school's main gate and refused to attend classes for several hours, demanding the appointment of additional teachers. Videos of the protest circulated widely on social media, bringing attention to the staffing issues at the school.

The protesters maintained that despite the school's inclusion under the PM SHRI scheme, the shortage of teachers was affecting classroom teaching and learning. They urged the education department to fill vacant posts at the earliest.

Following the demonstration, education authorities engaged with the students and local residents. Reports indicate that five teachers were deployed to the school after the protest, although officials have not announced whether these appointments are permanent.

The incident has renewed discussions on teacher vacancies in government schools and the importance of ensuring that educational infrastructure is supported by adequate teaching staff to provide quality education.

title: Flight Crisis Deepens in Andaman as Congress Leader TSG Bhasker Raises Alarm Over Reduced Services and High Fares
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Congress leader TSG Bhasker raises concerns over reduced flights and high airfares affecting tourism, businesses, e-commerce and patients in Andaman.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 31, 2026

Congress political leader Shri TSG Bhasker has raised serious concerns over the ongoing shortage of flight services to and from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, highlighting the impact of reduced connectivity and rising airfares on tourism, local businesses, e-commerce and patients travelling to the mainland.

Speaking during a press interaction, Bhasker described the situation as unprecedented, claiming that even during the COVID-19 period, the Islands had not witnessed such a prolonged disruption in air connectivity.

“Even during COVID, we had not seen a situation like this.”

He pointed to the limited number of flights currently operating and the sharp rise in airfares, arguing that the consequences are being felt across the wider Island economy.

Tourism Industry Under Pressure

According to TSG Bhasker, reduced flight services are directly affecting the tourism sector.

He said the impact extends beyond hotels and tourism operators to businesses dependent on tourist arrivals, while high airfares are making travel to the Islands increasingly difficult.

E-Commerce Deliveries Affected

Bhasker also highlighted the effect on e-commerce.

He said mainland-ordered goods are reportedly taking significantly longer to reach the Islands, adding that the geographical isolation of the Union Territory makes dependable air connectivity particularly important.

Unlike mainland regions, the Islands do not have extensive road and railway alternatives for mainland connectivity.

“If we had railways or road transport as alternatives, the situation would have been different. But for the Islands, air connectivity is essential.”

“Writing Letters Is Not Enough”

Bhasker also questioned whether repeated representations by organisations such as the Chamber of Commerce were producing tangible results.

He argued that submitting letters is only the beginning and called for sustained follow-up with the Administration and airlines until concrete outcomes are achieved.

“Writing letters is not enough. There has to be follow-up and pressure until there is a result.”

He also referred to previous interventions by industry bodies on issues affecting the Islands and stressed the importance of continuing to pursue such matters until they are resolved.

Patients Among the Worst Affected

One of the most serious concerns raised by Bhasker was the financial burden faced by patients who need specialised treatment on the mainland.

He claimed that some patients could face expenses of around ₹4.5 lakh for travel and related arrangements.

Bhasker appealed to the Administration to consider using a portion of medical or welfare funds to assist patients with transportation costs.

“If a patient has to spend ₹4.5 lakh just to travel for treatment, what will they be able to afford after reaching the mainland?”

He further raised concerns that families could be forced to sell jewellery or other assets to meet emergency medical travel expenses.

As a possible measure, he suggested a dedicated annual allocation to support transportation for a limited number of patients requiring mainland treatment.


Four Months of Connectivity Concerns

Bhasker also highlighted concerns over the period between June and September, arguing that the prolonged reduction in flight availability was effectively isolating the Islands during a crucial period.

While flights continue to operate intermittently, he argued that the present level of connectivity remains inadequate for the requirements of residents and the local economy.

The issue, therefore, extends beyond the aviation sector.

It affects tourism, commerce, online shopping, healthcare and everyday connectivity.

The Bigger Question: Who Pays the Price?

For the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, air connectivity is not simply a matter of convenience.

The absence of mainland road and railway alternatives makes reliable air services particularly important for residents, businesses and patients.

When flights become fewer and fares rise, the consequences can be felt across the Islands.

TSG Bhasker has called for urgent intervention by the Administration and concerned authorities to restore adequate flight capacity, address high airfares and ensure that patients and other essential travellers are not priced out of mainland connectivity.

For an island territory with no mainland road or railway alternative, how long can Islanders be expected to pay the price for inadequate air connectivity?

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

Editor's Note: The ₹4.5 lakh patient-travel figure and other statements attributed to Shri TSG Bhasker are presented as claims made during the press interaction and have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

title: Coach Reflects on R. Vaishali’s Rise to Women’s World Championship Contender
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Coach R.B. Ramesh reflects on R. Vaishali’s journey from a young chess enthusiast to a Women’s World Championship contender.
html:
April 18, 2026 | New Delhi

The journey of Indian chess player R. Vaishali from a young enthusiast to a Women’s World Championship challenger has been marked by discipline, resilience, and strong mentorship, according to her long-time coach R.B. Ramesh. Having trained her for over a decade, Ramesh offered insights into both her professional growth and personal character, highlighting the sustained effort behind her rise on the global stage.

Recalling a recent tournament in Cyprus where Vaishali was on the brink of a major victory, Ramesh described an emotional moment when he arrived just in time to witness her stepping onto the stage. The moment reflected the culmination of years of hard work and shared commitment between coach and player. According to him, such milestones represent not just competitive success but also the emotional weight of a long journey.

Ramesh traced the origins of this journey back to 2014, when he first connected with Vaishali’s family. Recognising the potential in both Vaishali and her younger brother R Praggnanandhaa, he agreed to train them. What followed was an intense daily routine, with the siblings travelling long distances to attend training sessions that spanned most of the day. Their disciplined schedule and commitment to practice played a crucial role in shaping their careers.

The coach emphasised the strong work ethic demonstrated by both players, noting their willingness to dedicate long hours without excuses. He also acknowledged the role of their early mentor Thiyagrajan in instilling a deep passion for the game, crediting him for laying a solid foundation that later training could build upon.

Discussing Vaishali’s playing style, Ramesh highlighted a balance between technical strength and emotional sensitivity. While capable of high-level positional play, she has at times been affected by the psychological pressures of competition. To address this, the support team adopted measures to maintain a positive environment during crucial tournaments, including involving fellow player Pranesh M to help ease tension and keep morale high.

Beyond competitive ability, Ramesh pointed to Vaishali’s integrity as a defining trait. He recalled instances where she chose fairness over potential advantage, underlining her adherence to ethical standards in the sport. This, he suggested, sets her apart in an increasingly competitive landscape.

Ramesh also highlighted the importance of family support in her journey, noting that her parents maintained trust in the training process and avoided interference in technical decisions. This collaborative dynamic between player, coach, and family created a stable environment for growth.

As Vaishali prepares to face reigning world champion Ju Wenjun, Ramesh acknowledged the challenge ahead but expressed confidence in her readiness. He indicated that her progression reflects years of preparation and belief, adding that both Vaishali and her brother have long carried the ambition of reaching the pinnacle of world chess.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume IX, Issue No. 1.
