title: MP Bishnu Pada Ray Urges Union Health Minister to Strengthen Healthcare Facilities Across Andaman & Nicobar Islands
author: Dweep Tulika
description: MP Bishnu Pada Ray has urged Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda to strengthen healthcare facilities at Diglipur Hospital and review medical infrastructu
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar Islands | 01 August 2026

Member of Parliament from the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Bishnu Pada Ray, has urged Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda to strengthen healthcare facilities at the Sub-District Hospital, Diglipur, and undertake a comprehensive review of medical infrastructure across the Islands.

In a letter addressed to the Union Health Minister, the MP sought urgent measures to improve healthcare services at the Diglipur hospital and requested a detailed assessment of all District Hospitals, Sub-District Hospitals, Community Health Centres (CHCs), Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Health & Wellness Centres across the Union Territory.

According to the representation, the Sub-District Hospital at Diglipur was established by upgrading the Community Health Centre following an announcement made by the Prime Minister during his visit to Sri Vijaya Puram on 30 December 2018. The MP stated that although the hospital was upgraded to cater to the growing healthcare needs of North Andaman, several essential facilities remain unavailable.

The representation states that the hospital is facing shortages of specialist doctors, general physicians, radiologists, healthcare professionals, medicines, laboratory equipment, diagnostic facilities and sanitation staff. According to the MP, these deficiencies compel patients from Diglipur and neighbouring areas to travel to G.B. Pant Hospital, Sri Vijaya Puram, even for routine specialist consultations and diagnostic services, resulting in financial hardship for patients while increasing pressure on the referral hospital.

Bishnu Pada Ray further stated that similar shortages of doctors, medical staff, medicines and diagnostic facilities also exist in the District Hospitals at Mayabunder and Car Nicobar, as well as in several Community Health Centres, Primary Health Centres and Health & Wellness Centres across the Islands. He said these shortcomings have persisted for a considerable period and require immediate attention.

The MP requested the Union Health Minister to personally intervene and direct a comprehensive review of healthcare infrastructure across the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. He urged the Ministry to fill vacant medical and paramedical posts, strengthen diagnostic and treatment facilities, ensure the regular availability of essential medicines, provide adequate laboratory equipment and supporting staff, and improve healthcare infrastructure to make quality medical services more accessible across the Islands.

Copies of the representation have also been forwarded to the Union Home Minister, the Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and the Chief Secretary of the A&N Administration, requesting their intervention for the early resolution of healthcare issues affecting island residents.

title: Ram Rahim’s ‘Facts vs Fiction’: What the Court Record Actually Says
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Ram Rahim remains convicted in the 2017 rape case, while two murder convictions were overturned and another criminal prosecution remains pending.
html:
A fact-check of a Dera Sacha Sauda publicity campaign defending its chief amid a standing rape conviction and pending criminal proceedings

By Dweep Tulika

A full-page advertisement published on September 12, 2026, in The Hindu and Dainik Bhaskar presents Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh through a familiar narrative of conspiracy, alleged false witnesses and misinformation.

The advertisement is titled “What is Dera Sacha Sauda? — Facts vs Fiction.”

The Hindu has stated in a disclaimer that it had no editorial or journalistic involvement in the creative or content of the advertisement.

But when the advertisement's claims are placed alongside the judicial record, the picture is more complicated.

The issue is not whether Ram Rahim's followers believe in him or whether Dera Sacha Sauda has undertaken charitable or social-service activities.

The relevant question is:

What has actually been established by courts, what has been overturned, and what remains pending?

Here is what the current legal record shows.

CLAIM 1: “Ram Rahim has been falsely targeted.”

FACT CHECK: His rape conviction is not merely an allegation.

On August 25, 2017, a Special CBI Court convicted Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh of raping two women disciples.

He was sentenced to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, with two 10-year sentences ordered to run consecutively.

That conviction has not been overturned.

Ram Rahim has subsequently received multiple temporary releases from prison, but those releases have not cancelled the underlying conviction.

Therefore, describing the sexual-assault case merely as an “allegation” would be legally inaccurate.

At the same time, that conviction should not be used to imply that he has been convicted in every other criminal case brought against him.

Those cases have different legal outcomes.

CLAIM 2: “Repeated parole and furloughs prove that there is no special treatment.”

FACT CHECK: Temporary release is legally possible, but the frequency can legitimately be scrutinised.

Ram Rahim's latest temporary release came on August 25, 2026, when he was granted a 21-day furlough.

It was his 17th temporary release since 2020.

His releases in 2026 included a 40-day parole in January, a 30-day parole in May and the latest 21-day furlough.

Under the applicable Haryana prison framework, eligible convicts can receive parole and furlough subject to prescribed conditions and approval by the competent authority. Recent reporting cites provisions allowing up to 70 days of parole and 21 days of furlough in a calendar year.

Therefore, the fact that Ram Rahim has repeatedly received temporary releases does not itself establish that the releases were illegal or preferential.

But the frequency, timing and administration of those releases can legitimately be examined as a matter of public accountability.

The important distinction is:

A lawful temporary release is not an acquittal.

CLAIM 3: “The murder cases prove that the entire case against Ram Rahim was fabricated.”

FACT CHECK: The acquittals do not support such a broad conclusion.

Ram Rahim was convicted in the 2002 murder of former Dera manager Ranjit Singh.

In May 2024, however, the Punjab and Haryana High Court acquitted Ram Rahim and four others, finding serious deficiencies in the investigation and describing the CBI investigation as “tainted and sketchy.”

The CBI subsequently challenged the acquittal before the Supreme Court, which issued notice in January 2025. The matter remains pending.

Therefore, two statements would both be misleading:

“Ram Rahim remains convicted of Ranjit Singh's murder.”

And:

“The acquittal proves that every case against Ram Rahim was fabricated.”

The legally accurate position is:

He was convicted by the trial court, acquitted by the High Court, and the acquittal remains under challenge before the Supreme Court.

CLAIM 4: “Ram Rahim was convicted of journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati's murder, so that conviction still stands.”

FACT CHECK: It does not.

Journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati was murdered in 2002 after reporting on allegations concerning Dera Sacha Sauda.

Ram Rahim was subsequently convicted in the murder case.

However, the Punjab and Haryana High Court acquitted him in March 2026.

That is not the end of the legal proceedings.

In August 2026, the Supreme Court listed a challenge to the acquittal filed by Chhatrapati's son for final hearing. The Court observed that the acquittal required consideration.

The current legal description is therefore:

Trial-court conviction → High Court acquittal → Supreme Court challenge pending.

It would be incorrect to describe Ram Rahim as currently convicted of Chhatrapati's murder.

It would equally be incorrect to describe the matter as conclusively settled in his favour while the challenge remains pending.

CLAIM 5: “All criminal cases against Ram Rahim are over.”

FACT CHECK: No.

A separate prosecution concerning allegations of forced castration of Dera followers remains pending.

The CBI registered the case against Ram Rahim and two doctors and filed a chargesheet. The prosecution alleges that followers were subjected to castration in the belief that the procedure would bring them closer to God.

The broader allegations have involved approximately 400 men, although the number of identified victims/witnesses in the prosecution is considerably smaller.

Recent reporting confirms that the trial remains ongoing. In July 2026, the CBI told the court that one alleged victim who was also a prosecution witness could not be traced, affecting the progress of evidence.

This is therefore an ongoing prosecution, not a conviction.

The distinction matters.

It would be wrong to describe Ram Rahim as guilty of forced castration before a court determines the case.

It would be equally misleading to say that the case has been conclusively disproved or closed.

CLAIM 6: “The Dera's social work proves the allegations against its leader are false.”

FACT CHECK: Social service and criminal liability are separate questions.

The advertisement highlights Dera-linked social initiatives, including claims involving de-addiction, tree plantation, blood donation and records associated with social-service activities.

Those activities can be independently assessed on their own merits.

But charitable or social work does not establish whether a criminal allegation is true or false.

Likewise, the existence of a criminal conviction does not automatically invalidate every social initiative undertaken by an organisation.

The relevant question in a criminal proceeding remains:

What evidence was placed before the court, and what did the court decide?

Figures presented in a publicity advertisement should also be distinguished from independently verified statistics.

CLAIM 7: “If courts allowed him temporary release, he has effectively been cleared.”

FACT CHECK: No.

A parole or furlough does not erase a conviction.

Ram Rahim remains convicted in the 2017 rape case and continues to serve the sentence imposed in that case, subject to temporary releases permitted under applicable law.

His August 2026 furlough therefore does not mean that the 2017 conviction has been overturned.

This is one of the clearest distinctions in the entire debate.

Temporary release ≠ acquittal.

WHAT THE CURRENT LEGAL RECORD SHOWS

Conviction still standing

2017 rape case

Ram Rahim was convicted of raping two women disciples and sentenced to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment. That conviction remains the basis of his imprisonment.

Convictions overturned by the High Court

Ranjit Singh murder

Trial-court conviction → High Court acquittal in 2024 → Supreme Court challenge pending.

Ram Chander Chhatrapati murder

Trial-court conviction → High Court acquittal in March 2026 → Supreme Court challenge pending.

Still pending

Castration prosecution

A CBI prosecution against Ram Rahim and two doctors remains pending.

THE LARGER QUESTION BEHIND “FACTS VS FICTION”

The Dera advertisement asks readers to distinguish between “facts” and “fiction.”

But the public does not have to choose between a sect's narrative and its opponents' narrative.

There is a third option:

Read the court record.

The legal record does not support describing Ram Rahim as a person convicted of every crime alleged against him.

Nor does it support describing him as a completely exonerated spiritual leader whose entire criminal history was fabricated.

The record is more nuanced.

He remains convicted of raping two women disciples and is serving a 20-year sentence.

Two murder convictions against him were subsequently overturned by the Punjab and Haryana High Court, with challenges to those acquittals pending before the Supreme Court.

And a separate prosecution concerning alleged forced castration remains pending.

Those distinctions are not political opinions.

They are the distinctions that a campaign titled “Facts vs Fiction” itself requires.

BOTTOM LINE

The strongest myth to challenge is not the claim that Ram Rahim has never been acquitted. That would itself be false.

The real problem arises when an acquittal in one criminal case is presented as though it erased a separate conviction in another.

An acquittal in a murder case does not erase a separate rape conviction.

A furlough does not mean exoneration.

A pending prosecution is not a conviction.

And social-service claims do not determine criminal guilt or innocence.

The appropriate benchmark is neither a publicity campaign nor its political opponents.

It is the judicial record.

Dweep Tulika distinguishes in this report between convictions, acquittals, pending proceedings and allegations. The pending allegations should not be treated as established guilt unless and until determined by a competent court.

title: SFI Seeks Temporary STS Bus Diversion to JNRM via RGT Road
author: Dweep Tulika
description: SFI has urged STS to temporarily divert morning buses via RGT Road to JNRM amid traffic restrictions linked to the police recruitment process.
html:
Port Blair, September 10, 2026: 

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI), Andaman & Nicobar Islands, has urged the State Transport Services (STS) to temporarily divert college-timing buses through RGT Road directly towards JNRM College to ease difficulties faced by students travelling from southern parts of South Andaman.

In a representation dated September 10, 2026, addressed to the Director of STS, SFI State Convenor Abdul Warish said students travelling to JNRM from areas including Jirkatang, Namunaghar, Mithakhari, Ferrargunj, Tushnabad, Wandoor, Chouldhari and surrounding areas were facing inconvenience due to traffic arrangements linked to the ongoing police recruitment process.

According to the representation, STS buses carrying JNRM students are currently being dropped near Netaji Stadium, after which students have to walk approximately 2 kilometres to reach the college.

SFI said the issue is particularly difficult during the morning college hours between 7:00 AM and 9:00 AM, when students need to reach classes on time. It also highlighted difficulties during rainfall and adverse weather conditions.

The organisation has requested STS to consider a temporary diversion of college-timing buses through RGT Road up to JNRM between 7:00 AM and 9:00 AM, wherever operationally feasible, until the police recruitment process and associated traffic restrictions are completed.

SFI has also requested the Director, concerned STS officials and the concerned Sub-Division JE to intervene on an urgent basis.

The representation further seeks a written response from STS clearly indicating the decision taken on the request and details of any proposed arrangements.

In an email forwarding the representation to Dweep Tulika, SFI’s Com. Vishnu Manoj said the issue concerns hundreds of students travelling to JNRM from the southern areas and requested media coverage so that the matter receives attention from the concerned authorities.

The claims regarding the number of affected students, walking distance and current bus arrangements are based on SFI’s representation. A response from STS on the request was not included in the material provided.

title: “‘Someone Had Already Voted in My Name’: Sikar Voter Alleges He Was Denied Vote at Ward 45 Polling Booth”
author: Dweep Tulika
html:
A voter from Sikar says polling officials told him his vote had already been cast before he arrived. He alleges that he was repeatedly asked to wait and ultimately left without being allowed to vote. He also claims several other voters at the same polling location reported similar experiences.


Sikar, Rajasthan:

What happens when an eligible voter reaches a polling station, presents himself for verification and is told that his vote has already been cast?

That is the question raised by a voter from Ward No. 45 of Sikar Nagar Parishad, who has shared a detailed first-person account with Dweep Tulika following the circulation of a social-media video concerning the alleged incident.

The voter claims that he reached the polling station with his mother. His mother was allowed to vote first. When his turn came, however, he says polling officials informed him that his vote had already been recorded earlier that morning.

According to his testimony, officials pointed to a marking against his name and told him:

“You have already voted this morning.”

The voter says he immediately disputed this, stating that he had not visited the polling station earlier that day.

He also says he pointed out that there was no visible indelible ink on his finger.

However, the absence of visible ink by itself does not establish whether another person voted in his name. The matter would require examination of the polling records and the circumstances under which his name was marked.

What happens if someone has already voted in your name?

There is an important procedural question at the centre of the account.

The Election Commission of India states that when a genuine elector reaches a polling station and finds that somebody else has already voted in his name, the genuine elector can still be permitted to vote through a tendered ballot rather than through the EVM, provided the Presiding Officer is satisfied about the person's identity.

The ECI's polling handbook says the Presiding Officer should examine the identity of the person claiming to be the genuine elector through questioning and the identification documents produced. If satisfied, the elector is allowed to cast a tendered vote, with the prescribed record maintained in Form 17B.

That makes the voter's account particularly significant.

If his description is accurate, one of the questions requiring examination is whether he was offered the applicable tendered-ballot procedure after claiming that someone else had already voted in his name.

At present, Dweep Tulika has not independently established whether such a procedure was offered, whether it was applicable to this particular local-body election under Rajasthan's rules, or whether any tendered-vote record was made.

The alleged identification mismatch

The voter says officials subsequently checked details associated with the person who had supposedly already voted in his name.

According to his testimony, officials told him that the last four digits of the Aadhaar number associated with the earlier verification did not match his own Aadhaar details.

He says he produced his Aadhaar card and pointed out the discrepancy.

He further says he was willing to produce other valid identification documents, including his driving licence or passport, to establish his identity.

According to his account, officials nevertheless told him that no further identification was necessary and that nothing could be done because a vote had already been cast against his name.

He says he was asked to wait outside.

The Aadhaar-related allegation is particularly important but remains unverified. The actual identification document used by the earlier voter, what was recorded by polling officials and what identification was presented by the complainant would need to be established from official records.

Repeated requests for an explanation

The voter says he waited before returning to ask what would happen to his vote.

He says he was directed to the Booth Level Officer (BLO), to whom he explained the situation.

According to his account, the BLO directed him back towards the room where his verification had taken place.

He says he was again asked to wait outside.

Eventually, he says, he took his mother home and planned to return with his wife.

When he returned with his wife, he says she completed the verification process and was permitted to vote.

He then approached officials again.

His question, according to his testimony, remained:

If somebody else had already voted in my name, what happened to my vote?

He says he received responses including:

“We are looking into it.”

and

“Please wait outside.”

He further alleges that a police officer at the polling location behaved disrespectfully towards him and that he was eventually asked to leave through the gate.

These allegations have not been independently verified.

He says he returned to the polling station

The voter says he initially left because of professional commitments.

But he says the incident continued to concern him and he became worried that waiting until later in the day could mean his complaint would not receive attention.

He therefore says he cancelled scheduled work and returned to the polling location with members of his team.

According to his testimony, he was again stopped at the gate and told that he had already been informed that he would not be allowed to vote.

It was during this second visit, he says, that he encountered several other people at the polling location.

He claims that three or four people told him they had experienced a similar situation, alleging that they too had been informed that votes had already been cast in their names.

That claim is potentially significant—but remains entirely unverified by Dweep Tulika.

From one alleged incident to a wider question

Until his second visit, the voter says he regarded the matter as a possible individual error.

Hearing other people allegedly describe similar experiences made him question whether the problem might be broader.

He subsequently posted about his experience on social media.

According to his testimony, people responded with claims of similar experiences in other parts of Sikar, including references to Ward Nos. 43 and 15.

He also says he came across videos from other Sikar-based social-media pages discussing similar allegations.

None of those additional claims have been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

They should therefore not be presented as evidence of widespread electoral irregularity.

If independently established, however, multiple complaints from different polling locations would warrant examination by the competent election authorities.

Ward 45 was part of Sikar's civic election

The allegation concerns Ward No. 45 of Sikar Nagar Parishad, which went to the polls on September 11 as part of Rajasthan's second-phase urban local-body elections.

Published 2026 electoral-roll information lists 3,445 electors in Ward 45, divided across three polling parts.

More broadly, reports from Rajasthan on polling day said allegations of bogus voting and clashes were reported in several places, including Sikar.

Those reports, however, do not establish the allegations made by this particular voter.

The two matters should not be conflated.

The questions that require answers

The testimony raises several questions that can be answered only through official records:

  • How was the voter's name marked as having already voted?
  • Who was recorded as having voted against his electoral-roll entry?
  • What identification document was presented by that person?
  • What identification details were recorded?
  • Did the identification details actually differ from those of the complainant?
  • Was the complainant's identity subsequently verified by the Presiding Officer?
  • Was a tendered ballot offered when he claimed that somebody else had already voted in his name?
  • Was any entry made in Form 17B, if the tendered-vote procedure was applicable?
  • Was the incident recorded in the Presiding Officer's diary or other election records?
  • Was CCTV/webcasting available at the polling station?
  • Were other voters at the same polling station recorded as having raised similar complaints?
  • Were any complaints of alleged impersonation or duplicate voting formally received?

The ECI's published election guidance specifically recognises the possibility of a person arriving after another person has already voted in that elector's name and provides for a tendered-ballot mechanism in such circumstances.

The applicability and precise procedure for the Rajasthan municipal election should, however, be confirmed from the Rajasthan State Election Commission and the relevant local-body election rules.

Not an allegation against a political party

The voter has not, in his written testimony to Dweep Tulika, attributed responsibility for the alleged incident to any particular political party or individual.

He says his purpose is to seek an investigation into what happened and to ensure that anyone who may have faced a similar problem receives an explanation.

That distinction is important.

At this stage, there is no basis in the supplied testimony to attribute the alleged incident to any political party.

The central issue is the integrity of the polling and verification process.

What Dweep Tulika has verified and what it has not

Dweep Tulika received the detailed account directly from the voter.

The account reproduced here represents his testimony and allegations.

At this stage, Dweep Tulika has not independently established:

  • who allegedly cast the earlier vote
  • whether impersonation actually occurred
  • what identification document was used by the earlier voter
  • whether the alleged Aadhaar discrepancy occurred
  • whether CCTV or other records corroborate the account
  • whether the voter was offered a tendered ballot
  • whether three or four other people experienced the same problem
  • or whether similar incidents occurred in Wards 43, 15 or elsewhere in Sikar.

Those questions require official records and responses from the competent election authorities.

The allegations therefore should not be treated as proof of electoral fraud unless independently established.

The question that now matters

If an eligible voter reaches a polling station and is told that somebody has already voted in his name, election procedure recognises a mechanism for dealing with precisely that situation.

The public-interest question is therefore not merely:

“Did somebody vote in his name?”

It is also:

“Once he claimed to be the genuine voter, was the prescribed procedure followed to verify him and, where applicable, allow him to cast a tendered vote?”

That question can be answered through the polling records.

Dweep Tulika will seek the response of the Rajasthan State Election Commission, the concerned Returning Officer/Presiding Officer and the district election authorities regarding the alleged incident and the procedure followed.

The allegations remain unverified unless supported by official records or other independent evidence.

title: Mukta Dhara Society and Dweep Tulika News Launch 'Clean Andaman Reel Challenge 2026'
author: Dweep Tulika
description: News invite residents to participate in the Clean Andaman Reel Challenge 2026 promoting environmental responsibility.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar Islands | 29 July 2026




















With an aim to inspire greater public participation in keeping the islands clean and environmentally responsible, Mukta Dhara Society, in collaboration with Dweep Tulika News, has launched the Clean Andaman Reel Challenge 2026.

The campaign, based on the theme "My Andaman, My Responsibility," invites residents of all age groups to create and share short Instagram reels highlighting the importance of cleanliness, environmental conservation and responsible civic behaviour.

Participants are required to create a 30–60 second reel and post it on Instagram by collaborating with @muktadharasociety. Entries may be submitted under any of the six categories: Before & After, Awareness, Art, Comedy, Cinematic, Children and Family Participation.

According to the organisers, the initiative seeks to encourage creative storytelling while promoting awareness about maintaining clean public spaces and protecting the natural beauty of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The evaluation will focus on creativity, the effectiveness of the message and the overall impact of the content.

Selected entries will be featured through the platforms of Dweep Tulika News and Mukta Dhara Society, providing participants with an opportunity to showcase their creativity while contributing to a social cause.

The winners of the competition will be announced on 15 August 2026.

The organisers have appealed to citizens, students, families, content creators and social media users across the islands to participate actively and spread the message that a cleaner Andaman begins with individual responsibility.

title: MP Bishnu Pada Ray Questions Government Spending Priorities in Andaman & Nicobar
author: Dweep Tulika
description: MP Bishnu Pada Ray questioned spending priorities, alleging basic infrastructure is being overlooked in the islands.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram, June 21:

Member of Parliament Bishnu Pada Ray has raised concerns regarding spending priorities in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, alleging that essential public infrastructure continues to face neglect while significant funds are being spent on vessels and facilities intended for administrative use.

Speaking at a public gathering, the MP questioned the need for expensive new vessels reportedly costing several crores of rupees. He alleged that despite persistent issues related to drinking water supply, road connectivity and other basic infrastructure in various parts of the islands, substantial expenditure was being incurred on assets primarily used for the movement and functioning of senior officials.

The parliamentarian also referred to frequent administrative changes and criticized what he described as insufficient focus on the everyday concerns of island residents.

According to Shri Ray, development priorities should be directed towards improving public services and addressing long-standing civic issues rather than funding projects that do not directly benefit the common people.

The remarks come amid continuing discussions on infrastructure development, governance and public expenditure in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Government authorities had not issued an immediate response to the specific allegations made by the MP at the time of publication.

Further details regarding the projects referred to in the speech were not immediately available. Independent verification of the expenditure figures cited by the MP could not be established at the time of publication.

The issue is likely to contribute to wider debate on development priorities and allocation of public resources in the islands.

title: Ashneer Grover Questions New UPI Charges: Who Will Ultimately Pay?
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Ashneer Grover questions whether new UPI MDR costs could eventually reach consumers, while the government says customers will not bear the charge.
html:
New 0.4% MDR applies to specified merchant payments above ₹2,000 from October 15; government says consumers cannot be charged, while Grover argues the cost could eventually reach them indirectly

New Delhi, September 16, 2026:


The introduction of a new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on certain higher-value UPI merchant payments has triggered a debate over who ultimately bears the cost.

Among those questioning the move is entrepreneur and BharatPe co-founder Ashneer Grover, who has argued that even if the charge is formally imposed on merchants, businesses may eventually recover the cost through prices or other changes affecting consumers.

Under the new framework, effective October 15, 2026, a 0.4% MDR will apply to specified person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI payments above ₹2,000, with the charge capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. Person-to-person UPI payments will remain free regardless of amount. Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through eligible UPI QR transactions will also remain under a zero-MDR arrangement.

The government has also said UPI providers cannot impose additional charges on users and has advised banks to ensure that merchants do not pass the MDR on to customers.

That is where Grover's question begins:

Who really pays?

Grover's argument: the cost can eventually reach consumers

Grover's argument is based on a basic feature of business economics: a cost imposed on a business does not necessarily remain entirely with the business.

In a television interview, Grover questioned the government's assurance that consumers would remain unaffected, arguing that “end of day consumer pays.” He has also argued that a levy associated with UPI should effectively be regarded as a form of tax collection.

His argument does not mean that customers will receive a separate UPI bill.

The question is about indirect costs.

For example, if a merchant receives a ₹10,000 UPI payment, a 0.4% MDR would amount to ₹40. The merchant would formally bear that charge.

The merchant could absorb the ₹40 as a business expense. Alternatively, depending on the business and its margins, the merchant could respond by changing prices, encouraging another payment method or adjusting other costs.

Whether merchants actually pass the cost on to consumers remains an open question, rather than an established outcome.

What does the government say?

The government's position is different.

The new framework is designed to create a revenue model for the UPI ecosystem while keeping ordinary users protected. The government says the MDR will be distributed among participants in the payment ecosystem, including banks and payment-app providers.

The framework also contains several exemptions and reduced charges.

For example:

  • P2P UPI payments remain free, regardless of amount.
  • Standard P2M payments up to ₹2,000 remain outside the MDR.
  • Eligible small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month through UPI QR transactions remain exempt.
  • Certain sectors including railways, telecom, insurance and fuel have a ₹5 flat MDR for specified transactions above ₹2,000.
  • Certain capital-market transactions will attract a lower 0.02% MDR, capped at ₹300.

The government says only about 4% of merchant transactions are expected to be affected by the new MDR because most transactions fall below ₹2,000 or within the zero-MDR small-merchant framework.

Why charge UPI after years of free payments?

Grover has also questioned the economic rationale for introducing charges after UPI's growth was built around the convenience of a largely free payment system.

His broader argument is that digital payments may reduce some of the costs associated with cash-based transactions, including cash handling and physical payment infrastructure.

He has therefore questioned whether those wider economic benefits should be considered when assessing the cost of maintaining UPI. Reports of his comments also show him pointing to the cost of India's ATM and cash-logistics network while questioning the rationale for charging UPI.

The government and payment ecosystem have a different economic argument: UPI requires continued investment in infrastructure, cybersecurity, innovation and service capacity, and a sustainable commercial model could help finance that expansion.

So the disagreement is not simply about whether UPI costs money.

It is about who should bear those costs and how the economic benefits of digital payments should be accounted for.

Could ordinary consumers eventually feel the impact?

This is the most important distinction in the debate.

Consider a ₹20,000 purchase.

At 0.4%, the MDR would be:

₹20,000 × 0.4% = ₹80

Under the new rules, the customer is not supposed to pay that ₹80 as a separate UPI charge.

The merchant bears the MDR.

But what happens afterwards is an economic question.

One merchant may absorb the cost.

Another may accept a slightly lower margin.

Another could change prices.

Another could encourage customers to use cash or another payment method.

There is currently no evidence that all merchants will pass the cost to customers. Equally, the government's prohibition on directly passing the MDR to customers does not by itself establish how individual businesses will adjust their broader pricing decisions.

That is the gap between the government's direct-charge assurance and Grover's indirect-cost argument.

Is the MDR a tax?

This is another area where the distinction matters.

Grover has described the levy as effectively “tax collection.”

The government's framework, however, treats the MDR as a merchant-payment charge within the UPI ecosystem, with proceeds distributed among payment-system participants. The government has not described the MDR itself as a tax collected from consumers.

Therefore, calling the MDR a “tax” is Grover's characterization, not the government's description of the mechanism.

What changes for ordinary UPI users?

For most people, the immediate change is narrower than the headline “UPI charges” might suggest.

If someone sends money to a friend or family member through UPI, there is no new charge.

If a customer makes a merchant payment within the applicable free threshold, there is also no MDR.

The new charge primarily concerns specified P2M transactions above ₹2,000.

The practical question for consumers will therefore be less about receiving a UPI bill and more about whether merchants change prices, payment preferences or business practices after the MDR takes effect.

The real test begins October 15

UPI has become deeply integrated into everyday economic activity in India, from small purchases to large merchant payments.

The new MDR framework attempts to address the financial sustainability of the payment ecosystem while protecting consumers from a direct transaction fee.

Grover's criticism raises a different question: Can a cost imposed on merchants remain entirely with merchants in a competitive economy, or will some of it eventually be reflected elsewhere?

There is no established answer yet.

The government has explicitly said customers should not bear the MDR. Grover argues that business costs can ultimately reach consumers.

The evidence on how merchants actually respond will only emerge after the framework takes effect on October 15.

title: Census 2026: Understanding India’s Largest Administrative Exercise Beyond Just Numbers
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Census 2026 will be India’s largest administrative exercise, shaping governance, planning, welfare and demographic analysis nationwide.
html:
Sri Vijayapuram, 20 April 2026:

India is preparing to undertake Census 2026, widely regarded as the world’s largest administrative exercise, aimed at creating an extensive demographic snapshot of the country’s population.

Conducted under the provisions of the Census Act, 1948, the exercise extends far beyond a simple population count. It seeks to document how people live, work and interact across the country, providing critical data for governance, development planning and public policy formulation.

In formal terms, a census refers to the systematic process of collecting, compiling and recording information about every individual within a defined population. Conducted once every decade, the exercise involves enumerators reaching households across highly diverse terrains—from metropolitan cities and Himalayan regions to remote island territories such as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The central objective remains universal inclusion, ensuring that no individual remains uncounted irrespective of geography or socio-economic background.

The importance of the census lies in its role as a foundational pillar of governance. Data generated through the exercise influences policy decisions across multiple sectors, including infrastructure development, welfare schemes, education, healthcare and resource distribution.

Census data also plays a significant role in democratic processes, particularly in constituency delimitation and political representation, while simultaneously supporting economic planning and long-term developmental strategies.

The census process operates on several established principles designed to ensure consistency and reliability:

• Individual Enumeration — Every person is counted separately rather than only as part of a household
• Universality — Coverage extends across all regions and populations
• Simultaneity — Data collection occurs within a defined timeframe, reflecting a specific national moment
• Periodicity — The census follows a decennial cycle

Together, these principles help create a consistent and comparable national demographic record.

India’s tradition of population data collection traces back centuries, with references to organised enumeration appearing in ancient texts such as the Rigveda and Arthashastra.

In the modern administrative framework, the first nationwide census attempt took place in 1872 during British rule, followed by the first synchronous census in 1881. This established the decennial system that has continued for more than a century.

For the first time in over 140 years, however, the census cycle experienced disruption due to the COVID-19 pandemic, resulting in the postponement of the 2021 census exercise.

Census 2026 is also expected to mark a major technological transition. India is preparing to conduct its first large-scale digital census using mobile application-based systems in place of conventional paper-based processes.

Experts believe that the shift towards digital enumeration could improve operational efficiency, reduce data processing delays and strengthen overall accuracy through real-time integration.

Observers continue to describe the census as the country’s most comprehensive and credible source of demographic information. Without such large-scale data collection, governance and policy planning would lack the empirical foundation necessary for informed decision-making.

From understanding population diversity to planning future development priorities, the census remains deeply connected to India’s administrative and developmental framework.

As preparations continue for Census 2026, the exercise represents far more than a statistical operation. It remains a critical instrument of governance, planning and inclusive development in a country defined by both its scale and diversity.

The success of the upcoming census will not only shape the quality of demographic data collected but also influence the effectiveness of policies and development strategies built upon it.

title: National Theatre Festival Marks 150 Years of Vande Mataram with Performances Across India
author: Dweep Tulika
description: National Theatre Festival 2026 celebrated the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram with performances across India, including Andaman.
html:
SRI VIJAYA PURAM, July 16: 

The Sangeet Natak Akademi organised the National Theatre Festival 2026 to commemorate the 150th anniversary of the national song Vande Mataram and Kalidasa Jayanti, bringing together young theatre artists from across the country in a celebration of India's cultural heritage and performing arts.

According to the organisers, the festival was held simultaneously at nearly 150 venues across all 28 States and 8 Union Territories. More than 4,000 young artists reportedly participated in over 150 theatrical productions presented in more than 39 languages and dialects, showcasing India's diverse theatrical traditions through folk theatre, puppet theatre and contemporary dramatic performances.

In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the festival was organised in collaboration with the Department of Education. Government schools in Sri Vijaya Puram, including Government Secondary School Junglighat, Government Model Senior Secondary School and Government Girls' Senior Secondary School, hosted student performances centred on themes of patriotism, freedom, national integration, sacrifice and constitutional values.

Teachers, students and members of the public attended the performances, which highlighted the role of theatre in promoting cultural awareness and civic values among young people.

The festival aimed to encourage greater appreciation of India's artistic traditions while reinforcing the message of unity in diversity through the performing arts.

Independent verification of the organisers' participation figures could not be established at the time of publication.

title: Manoj Paul Claims Calcutta High Court Issued Notice in PIL Alleging Government Land Encroachment
author: Dweep Tulika
description: calcutta-high-court-pil-lillipur-junction-encroachment-august-2026
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), Andaman & Nicobar Islands | 1 August 2026

Political activist and former Lok Sabha candidate Manoj Paul has stated that the Calcutta High Court's Circuit Bench at Port Blair has issued notice in a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by him concerning alleged encroachment on government land at Lillipur Junction.

Speaking outside the court after the hearing, Paul claimed that the matter relates to a building allegedly constructed on land previously occupied by APWD Quarters H-91 and H-92. According to him, the Court observed that a prima facie case existed and issued notice to the respondents.

Paul further claimed that the Court has sought responses from the Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, Chief Secretary and the Andaman Public Works Department (APWD) regarding the allegations raised in the PIL.

In his statement, Paul alleged that the construction involved encroachment on government land and also made allegations regarding the role of certain public officials in permitting such encroachments. He additionally alleged that several hotels across Port Blair had been constructed on encroached government land.

Paul said he was able to file the PIL based on information obtained through the Right to Information (RTI) Act, and thanked officials from APWD and the Revenue Department for providing documents.

He further stated that if the court ultimately orders action in the present case, similar alleged encroachments elsewhere in the Islands should also be examined.

At the time of publication, no response from Rajesh Anand or the authorities named in the video statement was available. The allegations made by Manoj Paul have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika, and the matter remains sub judice before the Calcutta High Court.

title: Three Indian Seafarers Dead After U.S. Strike on Tanker; Questions Raised Over Warning Claims
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Questions remain after a U.S. strike on MT Settebello reportedly killed three Indian seafarers.
html:
13 June 2026:

Questions continue to surround the U.S. strike on the oil tanker MT Settebello after reports indicated that three Indian seafarers lost their lives in the incident.

The vessel, a commercial oil tanker carrying 24 Indian crew members, was reportedly operating in the Gulf region when it came under attack by U.S. forces.

According to statements attributed to the United States military, the tanker was allegedly involved in transporting Iranian oil in violation of sanctions. U.S. officials have stated that multiple warnings were issued to the vessel before a precision strike was conducted.

However, the vessel's operator, UAE-based IOS Marine FZE, has challenged that version of events.

The company has reportedly questioned whether any effective warning was received by the vessel and has called for evidence supporting the claim that multiple warnings were issued before the strike.

The incident has attracted attention within India's maritime sector because it reportedly involved a vessel carrying a significant number of Indian crew members.

India has expressed concern over the deaths of its citizens and has sought details regarding the circumstances of the incident. Authorities have also emphasized the importance of ensuring the safety of Indian nationals working aboard commercial vessels in conflict-prone regions.

The deaths have triggered debate over accountability and the sequence of events that led to the strike.

At the center of the controversy remains a key unresolved question: whether adequate warnings were communicated to the vessel before military action was taken.

While U.S. officials maintain that warnings were issued, the vessel's operator has called for supporting evidence to be made public.

As investigations and diplomatic discussions continue, the families of the deceased seafarers continue to seek answers regarding the circumstances that led to the tragedy.

This report is based on publicly reported claims and statements available at the time of publication. Independent findings and official investigations may provide additional clarity as information emerges.

title: E20 Becomes a Political Flashpoint as Tehseen Poonawalla Questions Kejriwal’s Five-Day Ban Promise
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Tehseen Poonawalla questions Arvind Kejriwal's promise to stop E20 petrol in Goa within five days if AAP forms the government in 2027.
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | August 27, 2026

The debate over E20 petrol is increasingly entering the political arena, with Team Bharat's Tehseen Poonawalla questioning former Delhi Chief Minister and Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal over his recent promise in Goa.

Kejriwal has promised that if the AAP forms the government in Goa after the 2027 Assembly elections, his government would stop the sale of ethanol-blended petrol in the state within five days. He has presented the issue as one concerning motorists, fuel efficiency and consumer interests.

Poonawalla, who has himself been vocal against the implementation of E20, has questioned the practicality of such a promise.

His criticism raises a broader policy question:

Can a state government actually reverse or stop the implementation of a fuel policy within just five days of taking office?

The E20 Debate Enters Electoral Politics

E20 petrol contains 20% ethanol blended with 80% petrol.

The Centre has promoted ethanol blending as part of its efforts to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, support domestic ethanol production and lower emissions.

However, the policy has also faced criticism from motorists and campaigners concerned about mileage, vehicle compatibility, consumer choice and the impact on older vehicles.

These concerns have increasingly moved beyond technical discussions and into electoral politics.

Kejriwal has made E20 a potential political issue in Goa, giving voters a specific commitment to evaluate if AAP eventually comes to power.

But Can Goa Do It Alone?

This is where the political argument becomes more complicated.

The question is not simply whether a state government wants to stop E20.

It is whether it has the legal and administrative authority to do so independently, given the Union government's role in determining fuel specifications and ethanol-blending policy.

Therefore, Kejriwal's five-day pledge raises an important question:

What exactly would a future Goa government have to do to implement such a ban—and what powers would it actually have?

That question deserves a clear answer from any political party making promises on E20.

Poonawalla's Challenge

Poonawalla's intervention is significant because Team Bharat has itself been campaigning against E20.

His criticism therefore puts additional pressure on the political narrative surrounding the issue.

The debate should not merely become another exchange between political camps.

If motorists are being asked to choose between E20 and conventional petrol, they deserve clarity on:

  • Mileage
  • Vehicle compatibility
  • Pricing
  • Availability
  • Consumer choice

Similarly, if a political party promises to remove E20, voters deserve to know how that promise would be legally and administratively executed.

From Fuel Policy to Election Issue

Kejriwal's promise provides a straightforward electoral message:

Give AAP the mandate, and E20 will be stopped within five days.

Poonawalla's criticism raises the counter-question:

Is such a commitment actually within the powers of a state government, or is it primarily an electoral promise?

As Goa heads towards the 2027 Assembly elections, E20 could become much more than a fuel-policy debate.

It could become a test of how political parties address the everyday concerns of vehicle owners—and how realistically they translate campaign promises into government policy.

Ultimately, the public deserves more than slogans from either side.

If E20 is the problem, voters deserve to know exactly how it can be stopped. And if a five-day ban is possible, the political leadership should explain precisely how it would be done.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

title: Heavy Rain Lashes Mumbai, IMD Issues Orange Alert for City and Nearby Districts
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Heavy rainfall lashed Mumbai as the IMD issued an Orange Alert, warning of waterlogging and traffic disruptions across the city.
html:
Heavy overnight rainfall drenched Mumbai, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue an Orange Alert for the city and neighbouring districts.

Mumbai, June 24:

Mumbai experienced heavy rainfall on Wednesday following intense overnight showers that affected the city and several parts of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. In view of the continuing monsoon activity, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an Orange Alert for Mumbai and nearby districts, including Thane, Raigad, Palghar and Sindhudurg.

According to the IMD, moderate to intense spells of rain are expected to continue over the region, with the possibility of waterlogging, traffic congestion and disruptions in low-lying areas.

Rainfall data released by civic authorities showed that Mumbai received around 195 mm of rainfall between 8:00 a.m. on June 23 and 8:00 a.m. on June 24.

Among different parts of the city:

  • Mumbai City: Approximately 195 mm
  • Eastern Suburbs: Around 167 mm
  • Western Suburbs: Nearly 208 mm

The heavy downpour led to slow-moving traffic on several roads, while authorities remained on alert to respond to any flooding or emergencies.

The IMD has advised residents to remain cautious, avoid unnecessary travel during periods of intense rainfall and follow updates issued by local authorities.

With the southwest monsoon remaining active over Maharashtra, intermittent heavy showers are expected in the coming days.

title: India’s Sugar Fight Gains Global Health Support as Anti-Obesity Measures Expand
author: Dweep Tulika
description: India expands anti-obesity awareness through Sugar Boards in CBSE schools as WHO promotes action against excessive sugar consumption.
html:
New Delhi | August 23, 2026

India’s efforts to address rising obesity and excessive sugar consumption have drawn renewed attention as the government promotes greater awareness of unhealthy dietary habits among children and adults.

A key initiative has been the introduction of “Sugar Boards” in schools affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). The boards are intended to educate students and parents about hidden sugar in commonly consumed foods and beverages and the health risks associated with excessive consumption.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has publicly welcomed the initiative, highlighting the importance of making children aware of their daily sugar intake and encouraging healthier choices.

The move comes amid growing concern over obesity, diabetes and other lifestyle-related diseases in India. A study cited by health experts found that Indian children may be consuming sugar at levels above international recommendations, with children aged 4–10 obtaining about 13% of their daily energy from sugar and those aged 11–18 about 15%.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends limiting free-sugar intake to less than 10% of total daily energy intake and says reducing it further can provide additional health benefits. In January 2026, WHO also urged governments worldwide to strengthen taxes on sugary drinks as part of efforts to tackle obesity, diabetes and other non-communicable diseases.

India’s approach has therefore attracted attention because it combines public awareness with broader policy measures. The government has also encouraged reductions in excessive oil and sugar consumption as part of its wider campaign against obesity.

However, social-media posts describing the development as “WHO applauding the Modi government” require qualification. There is no clear WHO statement located so far specifically using that language to endorse India’s Sugar Board initiative.

WHO’s documented position does support stronger action to reduce excessive sugar consumption and promote healthier food environments, but this should not automatically be presented as a specific endorsement of the Indian government's Sugar Board programme.

The growing focus on sugar reflects a wider shift in India’s public-health debate—from addressing obesity and diabetes primarily after they develop to encouraging preventive action, particularly among children.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

title: Roadwork During School Hours Raises Safety Concerns Among Residents in Andaman
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Residents raise concerns over road construction during school dispersal hours, urging safer scheduling of roadworks in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
html:
SRI VIJAYA PURAM, July 22:

Road construction and resurfacing works underway across several parts of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have prompted public concern over the timing of such projects, particularly when heavy machinery operates during school dispersal hours.

According to observations and concerns expressed by residents, a road construction site outside a school continued operating while students were leaving the campus. Heavy machinery, including a road roller, remained in use as children exited the school premises, leading some parents and commuters to question whether such operations could be temporarily paused until students had safely dispersed.

School dispersal periods are among the busiest times on local roads. Young children may not always be aware of the movement of construction equipment or heavy vehicles, increasing the importance of precautionary safety measures around educational institutions. While there is no indication that any accident occurred and no allegation that safety protocols were violated, residents have expressed concern that the proximity of heavy machinery to students could present avoidable risks.

Several members of the public have also questioned whether non-emergency road resurfacing and maintenance work could, where feasible, be scheduled during night-time or other off-peak hours when traffic volumes are lower. Supporters of this approach believe it could reduce congestion, improve public safety and minimise inconvenience to commuters.

Residents have suggested that authorities and contractors consider scheduling roadworks around school timings, temporarily suspending heavy machinery during student dispersal, deploying adequate traffic marshals and exploring night-time construction wherever practical.

Road infrastructure improvements continue to be welcomed by the public. However, many residents believe that careful planning and appropriate scheduling can help ensure that infrastructure development proceeds without compromising public safety, particularly the safety of schoolchildren.

Independent verification was established by "DT News" at the time of publication regarding the specific incident described outside the school.

title: CPI(M) Alleges Delhi Police Entered AKG Bhavan to Arrest SFI Leader; Police Cite 2021 Court Case
author: Dweep Tulika
description: CPI(M) alleges Delhi Police entered AKG Bhavan to arrest SFI leader Aishe Ghosh, while police say the visit was linked to a 2021 court case.
html:
New Delhi | 28 July 2026

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has alleged that Delhi Police entered its headquarters, AKG Bhavan, in New Delhi in an attempt to arrest Students' Federation of India (SFI) Joint Secretary Aishe Ghosh, leading to a confrontation between party leaders and police personnel.

According to CPI(M), the police team arrived in a private vehicle, with some personnel allegedly in plain clothes. The party said Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas questioned the officers' presence inside the party headquarters and asked them to produce the warrant, following which the police team left the premises without making an arrest.

CPI(M) General Secretary M.A. Baby described the incident as an unlawful attempt to arrest Ghosh and alleged that she had been under surveillance in recent days. The party also criticised the police action, describing it as an attack on democratic rights and linking it to the ongoing student protests.

Delhi Police, however, said the visit was connected to an old non-bailable warrant issued in a 2021 case pursuant to court orders and maintained that the investigating officer's visit was unrelated to the ongoing student agitation. According to police, the officer had visited AKG Bhavan only in connection with executing the court process.

The case is scheduled to come up before the court on 30 July. The incident has added to the ongoing political debate surrounding the handling of recent student protests and police action in the national capital.

title: Weather warning Alert in Andaman and Nicobar islands

Authorities have urged residents, fishermen, and coastal communities to remain alert and follow official weather updates and safety advisories issued by the concerned departments.
