title: ‘Baba or Babasaheb’: Neha Bora Sharpens Attack on Yogi Government During UP Student Yatra
author: Dweep Tulika
description: AISA president Neha Bora has stepped up criticism of the Yogi government during the GEN-Z Mahajutan Yatra, raising education, jobs and accountability
html:
AISA national president links education, employment and recruitment grievances to a broader political challenge during the GEN-Z Mahajutan Yatra

Gorakhpur/Lucknow, September 15, 2026: All India Students' Association (AISA) national president Neha Bora has stepped up her criticism of the Uttar Pradesh government during the organisation's ongoing GEN-Z Mahajutan Yatra, linking student and youth concerns over education, employment and recruitment to a wider demand for political accountability.

The sharpest political formulation attributed to Bora during the campaign has been her reported reference to a choice between “Baba” and “Babasaheb”, in an apparent contrast between Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Dr B.R. Ambedkar.

“Baba ka raj hoga ya Babasaheb ka raj hoga, aane wala chunav batayega.”

The statement has circulated on social media as a direct political challenge to the Yogi government. The exact wording is attributed to Bora in social-media reports; Dweep Tulika has not independently verified a full transcript of the speech.

The remark came amid AISA's statewide GEN-Z Mahajutan Yatra, which is being conducted as part of its broader GenZ Rising campaign.

From student issues to a broader political challenge

AISA announced the yatra in August as an effort to bring together student and youth concerns around education, competitive examinations, employment and social justice. The announced programme began in Prayagraj on September 9 and included stops in Rae Bareli, Varanasi, Azamgarh and Gorakhpur, followed by Lucknow and Meerut.

The campaign has focused heavily on issues affecting students and young job seekers.

In Varanasi, Bora raised concerns over university fees, paper leaks, hostel reservations, shortage of seats and scholarships, while also highlighting employment and recruitment problems faced by competitive-examination aspirants.

At an Azamgarh gathering on September 13, she criticised what she described as the “selling” of education through NEP 2020 and called for stronger public-school infrastructure, including teachers, laboratories and libraries.

Gorakhpur becomes the political backdrop

Bora's Gorakhpur appearance on September 14 added a more direct political dimension to the campaign.

Gorakhpur has a longstanding political association with Yogi Adityanath, who represented the constituency in the Lok Sabha for several terms before becoming Uttar Pradesh chief minister.

At the student gathering there, Bora accused governments of failing to adequately address concerns surrounding unemployment, recruitment delays, examination issues and education.

She also raised demands relating to scholarships, hostels, women's hostels and infrastructure funding in public universities.

AISA has said the campaign is intended to take student mobilisation beyond individual university grievances and build a broader youth movement.

‘Baba’ versus ‘Babasaheb’

The “Baba” and “Babasaheb” formulation gives Bora's campaign a distinctly political character.

“Baba” is commonly used by supporters and followers when referring to Yogi Adityanath, while “Babasaheb” is a widely used honorific for Dr B.R. Ambedkar.

By placing the two terms against each other, Bora's reported formulation invokes a contrast between the political leadership associated with the present Uttar Pradesh government and the constitutional legacy associated with Ambedkar.

That interpretation, however, is an editorial reading of the slogan. The precise political meaning Bora intended should be understood from the full speech and surrounding remarks.

The statement has nevertheless circulated widely on social media and has been interpreted by supporters as an explicit challenge to the political narrative surrounding the chief minister.

Education and employment remain the campaign's core themes

Despite the sharper political rhetoric, the yatra's stated focus remains student and youth concerns.

AISA has raised issues including:

  • unemployment;
  • recruitment delays;
  • competitive-examination grievances;
  • alleged paper leaks and examination irregularities;
  • university fees;
  • scholarships;
  • hostel shortages;
  • women's hostels;
  • public-university infrastructure;
  • teacher vacancies; and
  • concerns over the privatisation of education.

At Gorakhpur, Bora said student and youth movements were demanding accountability not only from university administrations but also from state and Central governments.

AISA has also sought to connect the current campaign with recent student mobilisation at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, presenting the Uttar Pradesh yatra as an effort to carry that momentum into the state.

Can student grievances become a wider political movement?

The political significance of the campaign will ultimately depend on whether the issues raised by AISA gain traction beyond organised student circles.

Unemployment, competitive examinations, recruitment, higher-education costs and access to public education directly affect large numbers of young people.

But the existence of grievances does not automatically establish the political strength of a particular student organisation or movement.

AISA will therefore face the larger challenge of converting individual student concerns into sustained mobilisation across Uttar Pradesh.

For now, the organisation is attempting to make education, employment and accountability central themes of its youth campaign while increasingly directing its criticism at the BJP governments in the state and at the Centre.

Bora's “Baba or Babasaheb” formulation has added an explicitly political layer to that campaign.

Whether the slogan becomes a wider electoral message—or remains a rallying line within a student mobilisation—will depend on how the campaign develops in the coming months.

Political balance

AISA's statements represent the position of a student organisation critical of the BJP-led governments.

The allegations and criticisms regarding unemployment, recruitment, examination irregularities, education policy and university infrastructure should therefore be presented as political claims and demands, rather than independently established failures of the government.

The Uttar Pradesh government's response to the specific allegations raised during the yatra was not included in the material reviewed for this report.

title: TMC Rebel Faction Announces New Leadership, Removes Mamata Banerjee as Chairperson
author: Dweep Tulika
description: A rebel TMC faction named Arup Roy as chairperson after declaring Mamata Banerjee removed from the post.
html:
A rebel faction of the Trinamool Congress has announced a parallel leadership structure, naming Arup Roy as chairperson while challenging Mamata Banerjee's leadership.

Kolkata, June 23:

A major political crisis has erupted within the Trinamool Congress (TMC) after a rebel faction announced the removal of Mamata Banerjee from the post of party chairperson and unveiled a parallel leadership structure.

The dissident group, led by Leader of the Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, held a meeting in Kolkata where senior party leader and former minister Arup Roy was elected as the chairperson of what the rebels described as the "real" Trinamool Congress. The faction also announced a 30-member national working committee to oversee the party's organisational affairs.

Rebel leaders argued that the previous organisational structure had completed its term and claimed that a fresh leadership arrangement was necessary in accordance with the party's constitution. They further stated that the newly formed committee would approach the Election Commission seeking recognition as the legitimate Trinamool Congress.

The faction also suspended several leaders aligned with the existing party leadership as part of its organisational restructuring.

However, the Mamata Banerjee-led camp has rejected the rebels' decisions, maintaining that she continues to be the legitimate chairperson of the Trinamool Congress. The party has also initiated disciplinary action against several rebel leaders while reaffirming its official organisational structure.

The developments mark the latest escalation in an internal power struggle that has intensified following the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections. Political observers believe the dispute could eventually require intervention by the Election Commission if competing factions formally stake claim over the party's organisational leadership.

The evolving crisis is expected to have significant political implications in West Bengal as both factions continue to assert their legitimacy.

title: TSG Bhasker Extends Financial Assistance to Two Patients Requiring Treatment Outside Islands
author: Dweep Tulika
description: TSG Bhasker provided financial assistance to two economically disadvantaged patients requiring treatment outside the islands.
html:
TSG Bhasker provided financial assistance to two economically disadvantaged patients who require specialized medical treatment outside the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Sri Vijaya Puram, June 21:

Continuing his humanitarian initiatives, Shri TSG Bhasker, Chairman of the TSG Charitable Foundation, extended financial assistance to two economically disadvantaged patients requiring specialized medical treatment outside the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

One of the beneficiaries, a resident of Sitanagar in Diglipur, is suffering from a serious eye disorder and has been referred to a mainland medical facility for advanced treatment.

The second beneficiary, a resident of South Point, is undergoing treatment for a kidney-related ailment and requires further specialized medical care in Chennai.


Recognizing the financial challenges faced by the patients and their families, Shri Bhasker provided monetary assistance to support their treatment and travel-related expenses.

While handing over the assistance, he conveyed his best wishes for their successful treatment and speedy recovery.

The TSG Charitable Foundation has been involved in various social welfare and humanitarian activities aimed at supporting individuals and families facing medical, educational and financial hardships.

The assistance forms part of the foundation's ongoing efforts to help vulnerable sections of society access essential healthcare and other support services.

title: ‘Verify U’ App Introduced in Andaman to Help Identify Unconscious Persons and Connect Them With Emergency Support
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Verify U has been introduced in Andaman with facial recognition, SOS, emergency contacts and restricted medical information features for emergency
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram | September 2, 2026

A new digital platform, ‘Verify U’, has been introduced in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands with the stated objective of helping identify people during emergencies and enabling quicker access to their basic, medical and emergency-contact information.

The application was demonstrated during an event attended by chief guest Nand Kishore Singh, Captain Saurabh and other guests and participants.

According to the developers, the platform combines facial recognition, emergency contacts, location services and controlled access to medical information, with potential applications in road accidents, cases involving unconscious persons, elderly people, children and women's safety.

Facial Recognition for Emergency Identification

One of the key use cases presented during the demonstration involved an unconscious person following a road accident.

The developers explained that identifying an accident victim and establishing contact with their family can sometimes take considerable time. They said Verify U is intended to allow another person to scan the face of a registered individual through the application and retrieve relevant identification and emergency information.

The presentation referred to a target of approximately one minute for obtaining such information.

The developers also highlighted potential applications involving elderly persons who become lost or confused and children who may be unable to communicate their identity.

According to the presentation, facial identification could potentially help reconnect such individuals with their families.

SOS and Nearby Emergency Alerts

The application also includes an SOS function.

During the demonstration, developers said that activating the SOS feature sends an alert along with Google location information to designated monitoring points.

They further stated that registered users within a five-kilometre radius could receive notifications, potentially creating a network of nearby people who may be able to respond to an emergency.

The broader concept presented at the event is to bring several emergency-related functions into a single platform.

Medical Information With Restricted Access

Verify U also includes a medical-information section.

According to the developers, medical information is intended to remain confidential rather than being openly accessible to every user.

They explained that access involves an OTP-based process and consent from registered family contacts before medical details can be provided to a doctor.

The stated objective is to enable medical professionals to obtain relevant information during an emergency while maintaining restrictions around sensitive personal information.

Questions Over Data Security

The use of facial recognition and personal information also prompted questions regarding data security.

The developers stated that information submitted through the application is encrypted and that the platform uses Amazon Web Services (AWS) servers in India.

They also said privacy considerations have been incorporated into the system.

These security and privacy claims were made by the developers during the event and have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

The Connectivity Challenge

An important question for the Islands is whether the application can function when internet connectivity is unavailable.

The developers acknowledged that the current version of Verify U operates online and therefore depends on internet connectivity.

They said work is underway to make the application lighter and potentially enable operation in environments with limited connectivity.

This could be particularly important in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where connectivity can vary between locations.

The Platform Depends on Public Participation

The developers said the effectiveness of Verify U would depend significantly on how many people register and keep their information updated.

Their stated vision is to build a sufficiently large user network so that an unidentified person encountered during an emergency has a greater possibility of being recognised through the platform.

Chief guest Nand Kishore Singh also shared a personal experience involving a medical emergency and difficulties in immediately connecting with family contacts.

He said such experiences highlighted the importance of accessible emergency information and expressed support for the initiative.

He also appealed to the media to create greater public awareness about the platform and encourage people to consider registering.

A Promising Concept — But Real-World Performance Will Matter

Verify U presents an ambitious proposition: using facial recognition, emergency contacts, location services and controlled access to medical information to create a common emergency-support network.

For the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, however, its practical effectiveness will depend on several factors:

  • Number of registered users
  • Accuracy of facial recognition
  • Internet availability
  • Data protection
  • Emergency response mechanisms
  • Accuracy and maintenance of user information
  • Coordination with emergency and medical services

The developers themselves acknowledged that the current version requires internet connectivity, making network availability an important consideration for wider adoption.

Claims regarding response times, medical benefits, security and technological effectiveness remain statements made by the developers during the event and will require independent evaluation as the platform is used in real-world emergencies.

The Real Test Begins After the Launch

Technology can potentially reduce the time between an emergency and identification of a person.

But technology alone cannot guarantee a successful rescue.

The effectiveness of Verify U will ultimately depend on whether people register, whether their information remains accurate, whether the system works reliably when needed and whether emergency responders can effectively act on the information provided.

For an island territory where connectivity itself can sometimes be a challenge, that practical test may be particularly important.

This report is based on the proceedings and statements made during the Verify U event. Technical, medical, security and performance claims made by speakers have been attributed and are not independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

title: Swatantra Bhardwaj Controversy: From Jantar Mantar Clash to Three-Week Interim Bail
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Swatantra Bhardwaj has received three-week interim bail in the Jantar Mantar assault case. Here is the timeline of the controversy and pending legal q
html:
A June confrontation involving a CJP protester’s father has grown into a wider legal controversy involving an alleged assault, SC/ST Act provisions, a separate POCSO case and threats against a minor activist

New Delhi, September 15, 2026: The controversy surrounding social-media figure Swatantra Bhardwaj has developed from a June confrontation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar into a wider legal dispute involving allegations of assault, caste-based abuse, online threats and competing claims over what happened during the confrontation.

The latest development came on September 15, when a Delhi court granted Bhardwaj three weeks' interim bail in the case concerning the alleged assault of Sanjay Azad, father of teenage CJP activist Nishu Aazad. The temporary relief does not amount to an acquittal and does not bring the criminal proceedings to an end.

The case has attracted attention because of Bhardwaj's social-media profile, his own statements about the confrontation, the subsequent invocation of provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, and a separate case involving allegations concerning a minor.

The Jantar Mantar confrontation

The matter traces back to a June 23, 2026 protest at Jantar Mantar associated with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP).

During the confrontation, Sanjay Azad, the father of teenage CJP activist Nishu Aazad, sustained a head injury. Bhardwaj was subsequently named in connection with the alleged assault.

The two sides have presented sharply different accounts.

The complainant's side has alleged that Bhardwaj assaulted Azad and that caste-based abuse was involved.

Bhardwaj, on the other hand, has maintained that he was himself attacked and that his actions were in self-defence. His lawyers repeated that position during the recent bail proceedings.

The competing versions have not been finally adjudicated.

The podcast that brought the case back into the spotlight

The controversy intensified after a podcast/interview featuring Bhardwaj circulated widely online.

In the video, Bhardwaj reportedly described having “cracked” or “cracked open” the skull of Sanjay Azad during the confrontation. NDTV reported that he also claimed the victim had received numerous stitches and suggested that political connections had prevented more serious legal consequences.

Those statements became a major catalyst for renewed demands for his arrest.

But there is an important distinction between the statement and the medical record.

Bhardwaj's description is his own account of what happened. It should not be treated as an independently established description of the injury unless supported by medical or other evidence.

How the SC/ST allegation entered the case

The legal character of the case also evolved.

During the September 14 bail hearing, the court specifically asked Delhi Police whether a casteist slur had been used during the confrontation.

According to reports of the proceedings, police told the court that the initial complaint did not mention a caste-based slur. A later statement recorded by police did contain such an allegation, following which provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act were invoked.

That sequence has become one of the issues raised by Bhardwaj's defence.

His lawyers have argued that the case and the subsequent escalation were politically motivated.

The complainant's side disputes that interpretation.

The truth of those competing claims will have to be determined through the investigation and judicial process.

Arrest in Uttar Pradesh and judicial custody

Following renewed demands for action, Delhi Police traced Bhardwaj to Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, where he was detained before being brought into the Delhi case.

The custody sequence then proceeded through the Delhi courts.

After an initial period of police custody, a Delhi court sent Bhardwaj to judicial custody. On September 7, he was remanded to 14 days' judicial custody, reportedly extending until September 21.

Bhardwaj also challenged his detention through a habeas corpus petition before the Delhi High Court.

The High Court rejected the petition, holding that he was in custody pursuant to judicial orders and indicating that challenges to the arrest should be raised before the appropriate trial court.

A separate case involving a minor

The controversy subsequently expanded beyond the assault case.

A separate FIR was registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, along with other provisions, in connection with allegations involving online threats and intimidation directed at Nishu Aazad.

However, the two proceedings should not be conflated.

During the September 14 hearing, the court was informed that Bhardwaj had been arrested in the FIR invoking the SC/ST Act and not in the POCSO case.

The allegations in the POCSO case remain subject to investigation and judicial proceedings.

Supreme Court intervenes over threats to Nishu Aazad

The controversy took another turn when the Supreme Court considered allegations concerning threats to the teenage activist and her family.

On September 10, the court took serious note of allegations that 14-year-old Nishu Aazad had received threats, including alleged rape threats, and that stones had been thrown at her home.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought status reports from Delhi and Uttar Pradesh concerning the FIRs, the security arrangements for Nishu and her family, and the action taken on the allegations.

The court stressed that the allegations could not be taken lightly and that a child and her family should be protected from intimidation.

The Supreme Court's intervention should not, however, be interpreted as a finding that Bhardwaj is guilty of the underlying allegations.

The protection proceedings and the criminal allegations are separate legal questions.

Bhardwaj's defence: self-defence and political motivation

Bhardwaj's defence has rejected the portrayal of him as the aggressor.

His lawyers have argued that the complainant's side initiated the physical confrontation and that Bhardwaj acted in self-defence.

During the recent proceedings, the defence also referred to video footage which it said supported that version.

The defence has further alleged that the prosecution is politically motivated.

Bhardwaj himself has denied using casteist language during the confrontation.

These are defence claims and have not been judicially established.

Political connections become another controversy

The podcast also brought political connections into the story.

Bhardwaj reportedly referred to political figures while discussing his alleged influence and claimed connections. Among the names mentioned was Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) leader Chirag Paswan.

NDTV reported that Bhardwaj also referred to Delhi minister Kapil Mishra while discussing political support.

The appearance of those names in his account does not establish that either politician was involved in the alleged assault or in any decision concerning his arrest.

Chirag Paswan has denied the alleged association.

This aspect of the controversy therefore remains a matter of competing claims rather than established fact.

Three weeks of interim bail

On September 15, a Delhi court granted Bhardwaj three weeks of interim bail in the Jantar Mantar assault case.

The order provides temporary relief while the criminal proceedings continue.

It does not determine whether Bhardwaj assaulted Sanjay Azad, whether caste-based abuse occurred, whether his conduct amounted to an offence under the SC/ST Act, or whether his self-defence claim will ultimately succeed.

Those questions remain before the judicial process.

Why the case has become bigger than the original confrontation

What began as a physical confrontation at a protest has now developed into a complicated legal and political dispute involving:

  • an alleged assault;
  • competing claims of self-defence;
  • caste-based allegations;
  • SC/ST Act provisions;
  • a separate POCSO case;
  • alleged threats against a minor;
  • political-connection claims;
  • social-media statements;
  • and questions over police procedure.

For CJP and supporters of the complainant's family, the case represents a demand for accountability over alleged violence and intimidation.

For Bhardwaj and his supporters, it represents what they describe as politically motivated prosecution and an attempt to portray self-defence as aggression.

The courts will ultimately determine the legal questions.

For now, the most important distinction is between allegation and adjudication.

Bhardwaj has received temporary relief through interim bail, but the criminal allegations against him remain unresolved.

title: ‘Meri Degree Ka Kya?’: Yuva Congress Andaman Raises Questions on Jobs, Vacant Government Posts
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Yuva Congress Andaman joins the “Meri Degree Ka Kya?” campaign, questioning vacant government posts, recruitment delays and youth employment.
html:
Campaign launched nationally on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday; Andaman leaders call for time-bound recruitment and ask what happens to degrees when educated youth remain without employment

Sri Vijaya Puram, September 18, 2026:
The Andaman unit of the Youth Congress has taken up the Indian Youth Congress’s nationwide “Meri Degree Ka Kya?” campaign, using a press conference in the Islands to raise questions about youth employment, vacant government posts and delays in recruitment.

The campaign was launched nationally on September 17, coinciding with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday. Indian Youth Congress leaders have demanded that sanctioned but vacant government posts be filled through a time-bound recruitment process. National reports on the campaign say the Youth Congress has cited 50,05,850 sanctioned government posts as vacant and has called for recruitment against these vacancies.

At the Andaman press conference, H. Yusuf, State General Secretary of the Youth Congress, said the campaign was intended to put the question of employment before the Prime Minister and the government.

‘What about our degree?’

Opening the briefing, Yusuf thanked members of the media for attending and explained that the Andaman Youth Congress was joining the nationwide campaign.

Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, Yusuf extended his birthday wishes to the Prime Minister before turning to questions concerning employment.

He referred to the BJP government's earlier employment commitments and asked what had happened to the promise of creating two crore jobs annually. He also questioned when vacant government positions would be filled.

According to Yusuf, educated young people were completing their degrees but continuing to search for employment. He framed the central question of the campaign as:

“Meri degree ka kya?” — What about my degree?

He said the campaign seeks to highlight the concerns of young people and families who invest significant amounts of money and years of effort in education with the expectation that a degree will lead to employment.

Diksha Dulhar: ‘What happens after the degree?’

Speaking after Yusuf, Diksha Dulhar, State President, Youth Congress Andaman, expanded on the campaign's employment-related concerns.

She questioned how young people could be expected to celebrate or participate in birthday-related activities when, according to her, many families continue to face financial pressure and young people struggle to find employment.

Dulhar referred to the financial sacrifices made by families to educate their children, including, as she described it, cutting household expenses and sometimes selling assets to fund education.

She questioned why government recruitment was not taking place when sanctioned posts remained vacant.

The campaign material displayed during the press conference cited 50,05,850 sanctioned government posts as still vacant. The figure is also being cited nationally by the Indian Youth Congress in its campaign.

The poster displayed at the Andaman briefing additionally carried the figure 34,25,00,000 applicants seeking jobs. That figure was presented as part of the campaign material; the Youth Congress's broader national campaign messaging similarly focuses on the gap between educated job-seekers and available employment opportunities.

Recruitment delays and examination concerns

Dulhar also raised concerns about recruitment and competitive examinations.

She referred to young people spending years preparing for examinations and said that even after completing their education, candidates can face uncertainty over recruitment.

Among the issues she raised were examination-related problems, recruitment delays and the absence of clear timelines for appointments.

The broader national campaign has called for a time-bound recruitment calendar, including defined timelines for recruitment examinations and appointments against vacant posts.

The issue has also been raised by Youth Congress units in other parts of the country as the campaign expands nationally. In Chandigarh, for example, the organisation similarly called for timely recruitment, transparent processes and clarity regarding examination results and appointments.

One-year deadline announced

A major part of the Andaman briefing was the Youth Congress's call for action within the next year.

Dulhar said the organisation was giving the government a period of one year, until the next Prime Minister's birthday, to fill vacant government posts meant for recruitment.

She said the Youth Congress would continue raising the issue during this period and warned that failure to act would lead to further public mobilisation.

According to national reporting, the Indian Youth Congress has similarly announced a year-long campaign around the issue and has said it will organise job marches and degree marches across the country. The organisation has also announced further protest action if its demands are not addressed within the stated period.

Call to Andaman's youth

Dulhar also appealed to young people in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to participate in the campaign.

She said the campaign has an online platform through which young people can submit petitions and access information presented by the campaign concerning vacant positions and employment.

The national campaign includes an online component through which the Youth Congress is seeking public participation.

The Andaman leaders urged young people to raise their concerns regarding employment and recruitment and to participate in the campaign.

A political campaign centred on employment

The “Meri Degree Ka Kya?” campaign is a political campaign of the Indian Youth Congress and its statements at the press conference represent the organisation's position.

The central issue raised by the campaign is the relationship between education, government recruitment and employment opportunities: young people obtain degrees and qualifications, while the organisation argues that vacancies in government departments remain unfilled.

The campaign's national launch has received coverage from multiple news organisations, with the principal demand being the filling of sanctioned vacant government positions through time-bound recruitment.

For the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the discussion also brings the broader question of employment opportunities for local youth into focus, particularly in a territory where government employment has traditionally been an important part of the formal employment landscape.

The Youth Congress's message from the press conference can be summed up in the campaign's central question:

“Meri Degree Ka Kya?”

The question, as raised by the speakers, is not limited to obtaining a degree but concerns what opportunities follow after years of education, examination preparation and financial investment by families.

Key Points from the Press Conference

Campaign: “Meri Degree Ka Kya?”
Organisation: Indian Youth Congress / Youth Congress Andaman
Andaman speakers: H. Yusuf, State General Secretary; Diksha Dulhar, State President
Main issues raised: Youth employment, vacant government posts, recruitment delays and examination-related concerns
Vacancy figure cited by campaign: 50,05,850 sanctioned government posts
Demand: Time-bound recruitment against vacant posts
Timeline demanded by Andaman Youth Congress: One year
National campaign: Launched on September 17, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday

Editorial Note

Dweep Tulika has reported the statements made during the Youth Congress Andaman press conference. Figures, allegations and political claims attributed to the speakers or campaign material have been identified as such and should not be read as independently verified findings by Dweep Tulika.

title: UN Watchdog Questions Great Nicobar Project, India Hits Back
author: Dweep Tulika
description: UN CERD has raised Indigenous-rights and environmental concerns over the Great Nicobar project, while India has rejected the committee's observations.
html:
New Delhi | August 27, 2026

A fresh confrontation has emerged between India and a United Nations human-rights watchdog over the proposed development of Great Nicobar Island, with the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) calling for suspension of the projects pending independent assessments, while the Government of India has rejected the committee's observations as “politically motivated” and “highly malicious.”

The development has brought the long-running debate over the Great Nicobar infrastructure project back into the national spotlight, placing Indigenous rights, environmental concerns and India's development priorities at the centre of the discussion.

In its concluding observations on India, CERD expressed concern over the potential impact of major infrastructure and development projects on Indigenous and tribal communities. With regard to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the committee recommended that India suspend implementation of the projects until comprehensive and independent assessments of their environmental, economic, social, cultural and spiritual impacts have been carried out.

The recommendation is particularly significant because the proposed Great Nicobar project is not a single infrastructure facility.

The approximately ₹92,000-crore project envisages a transshipment port, an international airport, a power plant and a new township, along with associated infrastructure and tourism-related development.

The project has been presented by the government as a strategically important initiative that could strengthen India's position in the Indian Ocean, develop maritime infrastructure and generate economic opportunities in the Islands.

However, environmentalists, researchers and sections of civil society have raised questions about the project's potential consequences for Great Nicobar's exceptionally rich ecosystems and Indigenous communities, including the Shompen and Nicobarese.

CERD's intervention adds an international human-rights dimension to those concerns. Its recommendation goes beyond asking whether the project is environmentally sustainable. It calls for consideration of the project's possible effects on the social, cultural and spiritual life of Indigenous communities.

India Rejects the Criticism

India has strongly pushed back against the UN committee's observations.

Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India's delegation had rejected what it considered sweeping generalisations and unsubstantiated allegations during the review process. The government also questioned the basis and approach behind several of the committee's observations.

India has reiterated that its commitment to combating racial discrimination remains unwavering and that the country possesses established constitutional, legal and institutional mechanisms for protecting vulnerable communities.

The government's response is significant because CERD's concluding observations are recommendations rather than legally binding orders. The committee does not have the authority to unilaterally halt an Indian infrastructure project.

Nevertheless, the recommendations have considerable international significance because they place the Great Nicobar project under renewed scrutiny from the perspective of Indigenous rights and international human-rights standards.

Development Versus Protection

The controversy ultimately raises a difficult question:

How should India balance strategic development with the protection of an extraordinarily fragile ecological and Indigenous landscape?

Great Nicobar is unlike a conventional mainland development site.

Its geographical isolation, biodiversity and Indigenous populations make large-scale transformation particularly sensitive.

For supporters of the project, delaying major infrastructure could undermine India's strategic and economic objectives in the region.

For critics, however, strategic importance cannot become a reason to dilute environmental safeguards or overlook the rights and interests of Indigenous communities.

The latest UN intervention therefore does not settle the debate.

Instead, it raises the threshold for answering it.

India now faces the challenge of demonstrating that the proposed transformation of Great Nicobar can meet the country's strategic objectives without compromising ecological integrity, Indigenous rights and the long-term interests of the Islands.

The government has rejected the UN committee's characterisation of the situation. The committee, meanwhile, has called for deeper and independent scrutiny before the projects proceed.

For the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the issue is no longer only about a port, an airport or a township.

It is about what kind of development the Islands are prepared to accept and what safeguards must accompany it.

Dweep Tulika | A Truthful & Unbiased Perspective

title: G. Bhasker Urges Lt. Governor to Personally Inspect NH-4 from Jirkatang to Diglipur
author: Dweep Tulika
description: ANTCC Campaign Committee Chairman G. Bhasker urges the Lt. Governor to inspect NH-4 from Jirkatang to Diglipur, citing road deterioration and pending
html:
Sri Vijaya Puram:

Chairman of the Campaign Committee of the Andaman & Nicobar Territorial Congress Committee (ANTCC), Shri G. Bhasker, has urged the Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands to personally travel along National Highway-4 from Jirkatang to Diglipur and assess the condition of the road and the difficulties faced by residents of North and Middle Andaman.

In a press release, Bhasker said NH-4, which he described as the lifeline of North and Middle Andaman, continues to remain in poor and deteriorating condition despite repeated assurances regarding its improvement and completion.

Bhasker recalled the Chakka Jam organised by the Congress Party on November 1, 2025, which, according to him, was subsequently called off following assurances concerning the improvement and completion of NH-4.

He stated that NHIDCL had subsequently assured in writing that pending road works would be completed by the end of June 2026. According to Bhasker, however, several stretches remain incomplete or have deteriorated even after the stated deadline.

Concerns over different NH-4 stretches

Bhasker highlighted the condition of several sections of the highway.

According to the press release, the Jirkatang–Middle Strait stretch has deteriorated at several locations despite earlier work.

Between Baratang and Kadamtala, Bhasker claimed that around 80 percent of the road is in good condition, while the remaining 20 percent is yet to be completed.

He further stated that approximately 40 percent of the Kadamtala–Parlobjig Gate No. 15 stretch has been completed, while the remaining portion is in poor condition.

The Parlobjig Gate No. 15–Bakultala Junction stretch was described by Bhasker as being in extremely poor condition.

Between Bakultala and Rangat, he claimed that around 40 percent of the work has been completed, with the remaining portion still pending.

Bhasker also raised concerns over stretches that he said had previously been completed. According to the press release, the Rangat–Billiground stretch has become severely dilapidated, with the road surface having opened up at several locations.

The Billiground–Mayabunder stretch was also described as badly deteriorated, with several locations reportedly lacking a proper road surface.

Bhasker further claimed that the Mayabunder–Diglipur stretch, which had previously remained in good condition, has now deteriorated significantly and poses difficulties for motorists and commuters.

Questions over quality and accountability

Bhasker said the continued deterioration of NH-4 raises questions regarding road construction quality, supervision, monitoring and accountability.

He argued that residents of North and Middle Andaman should not have to continue facing difficulties because of delays, poor execution or inadequate monitoring of an infrastructure project of such importance.

The Congress leader also raised concerns over what he described as a possible system in which road stretches are allowed to deteriorate until the applicable warranty period expires, after which fresh tenders are issued for repairs and maintenance.

Bhasker termed the alleged practice “high-level corruption.”

The allegation was made by Bhasker in the press release and has not been independently established by Dweep Tulika.

Appeal for first-hand inspection

Bhasker has therefore urged the Lieutenant Governor to travel from Jirkatang to Diglipur using NH-4, rather than relying solely on official reports and representations.

According to him, such a visit would provide a first-hand understanding of the difficulties faced by patients, transporters, tourists, students, workers and the general public travelling along the highway.

Copies of the letter, according to the press release, have also been forwarded to the Member of Parliament for the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, the Chief Secretary of the Andaman & Nicobar Administration, and the Executive Director of NHIDCL, Port Blair, seeking intervention and necessary action.

This report is based on a press release issued by ANTCC and reflects the claims and concerns raised by Shri G. Bhasker. The specific road-condition percentages and allegations regarding corruption have not been independently verified by Dweep Tulika.

title: Students and Leaders Protest Against Deemed University Proposal in Andaman
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Students and leaders in Port Blair held a candle march protesting the proposed Deemed University system for Andaman colleges.
html:
Port Blair, 25 February 2026:

A large candle march organised by the Joint Action Forum (JAF) witnessed strong participation from students, parents, and members of various political and social organisations protesting against the proposed Deemed University system for colleges in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

The march began from Flag Point and concluded at Tiranga Park, where a public meeting was held raising concerns over the future of higher education in the islands.

Addressing the gathering, Rakesh Pal Govind announced his resignation as an ordinary member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), expressing dissatisfaction over the handling of the issue. He stated that elected representatives who fail to address public concerns lose their moral authority to remain in power.

Govind alleged that the Deemed University proposal, which reportedly dates back to 2018, could weaken students’ access to quality education and further isolate island students. He also criticised recent incidents involving police personnel and urged authorities to review disciplinary actions and ensure accountability.

He stated that the movement would continue through peaceful and constitutional means, including legal action, public awareness campaigns, and delegations to New Delhi to raise the matter before national leaders.

Other speakers at the gathering questioned the need for a Deemed University system when alternatives such as a Central University could better serve the educational interests of students in the islands.

Speakers also urged the Member of Parliament to raise the issue in Parliament and stressed the need for responsive governance and accessible grievance mechanisms at the local level.

Leaders appealed to students to continue peaceful and disciplined participation, warning that failure to address the issue could lead to a larger island-wide movement involving schools and communities.

The protest concluded peacefully, with participants reiterating their demand for withdrawal of the proposed Deemed University move and protection of students’ educational rights.

Originally published in Dweep Tulika, Volume VIII, Issue No. 12, dated 20 March 2026.

title: Havelock Water Sports Resume After Talks With Administration
author: Dweep Tulika
description: Water-sports activities resume at Swaraj Dweep after talks between operators, boat owners and administration, while payment and operating issues remai
html:
Operators resume activities after temporary understanding; commission, staff-payment and long-term operating issues remain unresolved

Swaraj Dweep, September 15, 2026:

Water-sports activities at Swaraj Dweep (Havelock) resumed on Tuesday following discussions between local water-sports operators, boat owners, boat staff and the administration over booking arrangements, operational rights, licensing, safety requirements and livelihood concerns.

The standoff reportedly followed the establishment of a new booking counter operated by Blue Fly at the water-sports location. Local operators and boat owners objected to the arrangement, expressing concern that it could affect the existing system through which they operate and earn from activities including snorkeling and other marine tourism services.

Operators also raised concerns over commission-based earnings, particularly for boat staff whose income, according to stakeholders, includes commissions linked to water-sports activities.

Another point of contention was the reported restriction on certain licensed personnel entering the water. Operators questioned the restriction and argued that personnel holding valid licences should be allowed to perform their professional duties, subject to applicable regulations and safety requirements.

Safety compliance becomes a key issue

Safety was another major issue raised during the discussions.

Operators reportedly questioned whether all prescribed safety requirements, including necessary clearances and rescue arrangements, were being adequately followed in some activities. They stressed that marine tourism operations require strict compliance with safety protocols, particularly given the changing sea conditions around the islands.

The matter subsequently involved police personnel, local administration officials, boat owners and representatives of the operators' union.

Temporary understanding brings operations back

Following the discussions, a temporary understanding was reportedly reached, allowing water-sports activities to resume.

As part of the understanding, the disputed booking counter at the site was to be removed. Local operators would be permitted to resume operations, subject to valid licences and compliance with prescribed safety norms.

The administration also reportedly made clear that safety requirements could not be compromised and that violations could have implications for operators' licences.

Stakeholders were further urged to ensure that tourists were not inconvenienced or subjected to harassment during the transition.

Financial issues remain unresolved

Although the immediate standoff has ended, several financial and employment-related questions remain open.

Issues concerning commissions, TSC-related payment arrangements and salaries of boat staff are expected to be taken up separately with boat owners and other stakeholders.

This means that Tuesday's development appears to be an interim settlement rather than a final resolution of all the concerns raised by operators.

Swaraj Dweep remains one of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands' major tourism destinations, with activities such as snorkeling, scuba diving, kayaking and sea walking forming an important part of the island's tourism economy.

The episode has highlighted the need for greater clarity and transparency over booking arrangements, operational rights, licensing, commissions, worker remuneration and safety compliance in the water-sports sector.

For now, activities have resumed. Further discussions between the administration, operators and boat owners are expected to determine the longer-term framework governing water-sports operations on Swaraj Dweep.

title: Census 2026: India’s Digital Headcount Raises Questions Beyond Efficiency
author: Dweep Tulika
description: As India moves toward a digital Census 2026, experts raise concerns over data gaps, socio-economic realities and questionnaire relevance.
html:
Sri Vijayapuram, 20 April 2026:

As India moves towards a more digital and streamlined census process, discussions are intensifying over whether the evolving system is adequately capturing the complexities of real-life socio-economic conditions.

While Census 2026 promises improved efficiency through digital tools, self-enumeration systems and expanded verification mechanisms, experts continue to raise concerns regarding the depth, relevance and inclusiveness of the data being collected.

Traditionally, census exercises have focused on measurable household indicators such as housing conditions, family structure and ownership of physical assets. However, many observers believe that this framework is becoming increasingly limited in reflecting the lived realities of individuals and communities.

Critical socio-economic factors such as income levels, employment stability, quality of education, healthcare vulnerabilities and digital access remain only partially represented or entirely outside the existing scope of enumeration.

Experts describe this as a growing “data gap” with potentially significant policy implications.

Census data serves as a foundational resource for governance, influencing welfare schemes, infrastructure planning, budget allocation and long-term development strategies. Incomplete or insufficiently contextual data may therefore affect the accuracy of policy targeting and risk overlooking vulnerable populations.

The transition toward a digital census model has further highlighted structural concerns.

Self-enumeration systems assume access to digital devices, internet connectivity and a basic level of technological understanding—conditions that may not exist uniformly across India’s highly diverse population.

Observers caution that this could increase the possibility of incomplete or inaccurate entries, particularly in remote, economically weaker or digitally underserved regions.

Although enumerators remain responsible for verification and correction processes, experts note that verification mechanisms are ultimately limited to the data that has already been collected. Questions that are never asked—and realities that remain unrecorded—cannot be corrected during verification stages.

Another major point of discussion relates to the relevance of the questionnaire itself.

Critics argue that certain traditional indicators, including ownership of televisions or radios, continue to receive attention despite rapid socio-economic and technological transformation across the country.

At the same time, areas increasingly considered central to contemporary development—including digital access, financial inclusion, internet connectivity, skill development and access to welfare systems—remain comparatively underrepresented within standard census frameworks.

The shift from a fully enumerator-driven process toward a hybrid digital model has undoubtedly improved the speed and scale of data collection. However, experts argue that operational efficiency alone does not necessarily translate into deeper understanding of social realities.

According to observers, the broader challenge lies not only in how information is collected, but also in determining what information is considered important enough to record.

Verification processes may improve accuracy, but they cannot compensate for structural gaps in the scope of questioning itself.

As India prepares for Census 2026, discussions are increasingly focusing on the need for a more comprehensive, context-sensitive and future-oriented approach to demographic data collection.

With census findings shaping policy decisions, welfare allocation, infrastructure development and long-term governance strategies, many believe that the upcoming exercise represents more than a technological transition—it is also a test of whether national data systems are evolving in step with changing social and economic realities.
